def select_by_ao_projection(
    mf: Any,
    ao_labels: list[str | list[str]],
    projected_basis: str | None = "minao",
    contribution_type: Literal["r", "a"] = "a",
    contribution: float | list[float] | dict[str, float | list[float]] = 0.0,
    top_n: int | list[int] | None = None,
    restricted_space: _RestrictedSpace = None,
    save_path: str | None = None,
    *,
    return_contributions: bool = False,
) -> (
    np.ndarray
    | dict[str, np.ndarray]
    | tuple[np.ndarray, _AoContributions]
    | tuple[dict[str, np.ndarray], dict[str, _AoContributions]]
):
    """Select active orbitals by their projection onto a set of target AOs.

    Args:
        mf (pyscf.scf.hf.SCF or pyscf.dft.rks.KohnShamDFT):
            Mean-field object containing the molecular orbitals and occupation numbers.
        ao_labels (list[str | list[str]]): List of AO label entries. Each entry is either a single label string
            (e.g. ``"Fe 3d"``) or a list of strings treated as one group
            (e.g. ``["Fe 3d", "Fe 4d"]``). Entries can be freely mixed, e.g.
            ``["C 2pz", "Fe 3d", ["Fe 3d", "Fe 4d"]]``.
        projected_basis (str or None, default 'minao'):
            Basis set to use for the projection. ``None`` uses the original basis.
            A minimal basis (e.g. ``'minao'``) helps focus the selection on
            chemically relevant orbitals and reduces noise from diffuse functions.
        contribution_type ({'r', 'a'}, default 'a'): Relative (``'r'``, each group's weights divided
            by their maximum over the search space) or absolute (``'a'``) contribution.
        contribution (float, list of float, or dict, default 0.0): Threshold for
            selecting orbitals based on their contribution.
            A single float applies to all AO groups; a list specifies per-group
            thresholds and should match the length of *ao_labels*; on a length
            mismatch a warning is logged and the first value is used for every
            group. Ignored when *top_n* is given.
            For an unrestricted mean-field it may also be a spin-resolved
            ``{"alpha": ..., "beta": ...}`` mapping (each value itself a float or
            per-group list), applying a different threshold to each spin channel.
            A non-dict value is shared by both channels. A dict is rejected for a
            restricted mean-field.
        top_n (int or list of int, optional): Alternative to *contribution* thresholding. Selects the top N orbitals
            per AO group. A list specifies per-group counts; on a length
            mismatch with *ao_labels* a warning is logged and the first value is
            used for every group.
        restricted_space (list of int, list of tuple, tuple of lists, dict, optional):
            Orbital indices to restrict selection to. Can be a plain list of
            integers (e.g. ``list(range(34, 131))``), a list of ``(index, entropy)``
            pairs, or a ``(occ_list, virt_list)`` tuple from ``select_by_entropy``.
            For an unrestricted mean-field it may also be a spin-resolved
            ``{"alpha": ..., "beta": ...}`` mapping (as produced by
            ``select_by_spin_entropy``), in which case each spin channel is
            restricted to its own space. A non-dict value is shared by both
            channels. ``None`` considers all orbitals.
        save_path (str or None, optional):
            If provided, saves a heatmap of AO contributions to the specified path.
            For an unrestricted mean-field the alpha/beta channels are written to
            separate ``*_alpha`` / ``*_beta`` files.
        return_contributions (bool, default False): If ``True``, also return the
            per-group AO contributions so they can be passed straight to
            :func:`~aegiss.utils.plotting.plot_ao_contribution` for custom plots.

    Returns:
        active_indices (np.ndarray of int, or dict[str, np.ndarray]):
            Selected orbital indices. For a restricted mean-field a single array
            is returned. For an unrestricted (UHF) mean-field -- detected from a
            3D ``mf.mo_coeff`` of shape ``(2, nao, nmo)`` -- the selection is
            always done per spin (the AO overlaps are spin-independent, only the
            MO coefficients differ) and the result is a split
            ``{"alpha": ..., "beta": ...}`` mapping. Whether the two channels
            share one search space (spin-summed *restricted_space*) or use their
            own (spin-resolved dict *restricted_space*), the alpha and beta
            selections are kept separate here: they are deliberately *not*
            reconciled into a common set of spatial orbitals, since an orbital
            index refers to a different MO in each spin channel.
        ao_contributions (dict, only if *return_contributions* is ``True``):
            Group index (position in *ao_labels*) to ``(orbital_index, weight)``
            pairs over the whole search space. For an unrestricted mean-field
            this is a ``{"alpha": ..., "beta": ...}`` mapping of such dicts.

    Raises:
        ValueError: If *restricted_space* or *contribution* is a spin-resolved
            ``{"alpha", "beta"}`` dict but *mf* is restricted, or if an entry of
            *ao_labels* matches no AO of the projection basis.
    """
    logger.info("----------------AO Projection Screening for AEGISS----------------\n")
    logger.info("AO labels for projection: %s", ao_labels)

    logger.info("Contribution threshold: %s", contribution)
    logger.info("Contribution type: %s", contribution_type)

    if top_n is not None:
        logger.info("Top N orbitals to select: %s", top_n)

    if projected_basis is not None:
        logger.info("Using projected basis for AO projection: %s", projected_basis)
    else:
        logger.info("Using molecule for AO projection")

    _check_ao_labels(mf.mol, ao_labels, projected_basis)
    labels_idx: dict[int, str | list[str]] = dict(enumerate(ao_labels))
    mo_coeff = np.asarray(mf.mo_coeff)

    if mo_coeff.ndim != 3:
        if isinstance(restricted_space, dict):
            msg = (
                "A spin-resolved restricted_space ({'alpha', 'beta'} dict) requires "
                "an unrestricted mean-field with a 3D mo_coeff; got a restricted one."
            )
            raise ValueError(msg)
        if isinstance(contribution, dict):
            msg = (
                "A spin-resolved contribution ({'alpha', 'beta'} dict) requires an "
                "unrestricted mean-field with a 3D mo_coeff; got a restricted one."
            )
            raise ValueError(msg)
        resolved_contribution, resolved_top_n = _resolve_thresholds(
            contribution, top_n, len(ao_labels)
        )
        indices, contributions = _run_ao_selection(
            mf=mf,
            ao_labels=ao_labels,
            full_mo_coeff=mo_coeff,
            space=_resolve_space(mf, restricted_space),
            resolved_contribution=resolved_contribution,
            resolved_top_n=resolved_top_n,
            contribution_type=contribution_type,
            projected_basis=projected_basis,
            save_path=save_path,
            labels_idx=labels_idx,
        )
        return (indices, contributions) if return_contributions else indices

    logger.info(
        "Unrestricted mean-field detected (mo_coeff shape %s); screening the "
        "alpha and beta channels per spin (%s search space).",
        mo_coeff.shape,
        "per-channel" if isinstance(restricted_space, dict) else "shared",
    )
    selection: dict[str, np.ndarray] = {}
    channel_contributions: dict[str, _AoContributions] = {}
    for spin, channel in enumerate(("alpha", "beta")):
        logger.info("=============== %s channel ===============", channel.upper())
        # A dict restricted_space carries its own window per spin channel
        # (spin-resolved entropy screening); anything else is shared by both.
        channel_space = (
            restricted_space[channel]
            if isinstance(restricted_space, dict)
            else restricted_space
        )
        # A dict contribution carries its own threshold(s) per spin channel;
        # anything else is shared by both.
        channel_contribution = (
            contribution[channel] if isinstance(contribution, dict) else contribution
        )
        resolved_contribution, resolved_top_n = _resolve_thresholds(
            channel_contribution, top_n, len(ao_labels)
        )
        selection[channel], channel_contributions[channel] = _run_ao_selection(
            mf=mf,
            ao_labels=ao_labels,
            full_mo_coeff=mo_coeff[spin],
            space=_resolve_space(mf, channel_space),
            resolved_contribution=resolved_contribution,
            resolved_top_n=resolved_top_n,
            contribution_type=contribution_type,
            projected_basis=projected_basis,
            save_path=_channel_save_path(save_path, channel),
            labels_idx=labels_idx,
        )
    return (selection, channel_contributions) if return_contributions else selection

docs.title: AO label format
docs.text:
ao_labels follow PySCF's search_ao_label convention:

"C 2pz"                             # this shell on every (untagged) carbon atom
["Fe 3dxz", "Fe 3dyz", "Fe 3dz^2"]  # several orbitals in one group
"C.1 2pz"                           # only carbons labelled C.1 in the geometry

The Element.N form matches atoms whose label in the geometry is Element.N, such as the tags written by MolTagger. N is the tag you chose, not the position of the atom in the molecule. Tagged atoms are no longer matched by the plain element label: with a geometry containing C.1 and C atoms, "C 2pz" selects only the untagged carbons.

All four dataclasses are frozen (immutable) and validate their inputs on construction. Import them from the top-level package or from aegiss.config_dataclasses:

from aegiss import DMRGConfig, EntropyConfig, ProjectionConfig, OutputConfig
# or
from aegiss.config_dataclasses import DMRGConfig, EntropyConfig, ProjectionConfig, OutputConfig

Configuration dataclass for DMRG calculations.

Parameters:

Name Type Description Default ncas int

Number of active orbitals for the DMRG calculation.

required nelecas int or tuple[int, int]

Number of active electrons, either as a total count or an explicit (nalpha, nbeta) pair (same convention as PySCF's CASCI).

required max_bond_dim int, default 500

Target DMRG bond dimension (must be a positive multiple of 4). The sweep schedule starts at max_bond_dim // 2 and ramps up to max_bond_dim.

500 symm_type {'SZ', 'SU2'}, default 'SZ'

Spin symmetry used by block2. Both give spin-summed single-orbital entropies directly from the 1pdm/1npc output; 'SU2' is spin-adapted and faster. 'SZ' is required only for spin_soe='resolved' and for unrestricted (UHF) integrals.

'SZ' verbosity int, default 0

Verbosity level for block2 output. Higher values produce more detailed logs.

0 unrestricted bool or None, default None

Whether to emit an unrestricted (UHF) FCIDUMP. None autodetects from the mean-field type (isinstance(mf, scf.uhf.UHF)); pass True/ False to override. UHF requires symm_type='SZ'.

None reorder {'noreorder', 'fiedler'}, default 'noreorder'

Orbital ordering for block2main. 'noreorder' keeps the FCIDUMP order and enables full_fci_space; 'fiedler' reorders by the Fiedler vector and disables full_fci_space.

'noreorder' spin_soe {'auto', 'summed', 'resolved'}, default 'auto'

Whether single-orbital entropies (and the selection built on them) are spin-summed or spin-resolved. 'summed' uses the 4-state spatial entropy, so both spin channels share one entropy window; for a UHF reference the AO projection still returns a split {'alpha', 'beta'} active space. 'resolved' uses the per-spin-orbital entropies H(n_alpha) / H(n_beta) and screens the alpha and beta channels independently, yielding a split {'alpha', 'beta'} active space. 'auto' picks 'resolved' when the target is spin-polarised (nalpha != nbeta) and symm_type='SZ', else 'summed'. 'resolved' requires symm_type='SZ' (the spin-resolved 1-PDM is only available without spin adaptation).

'auto' Source code in src/aegiss/config_dataclasses/dmrg_config.py 
@dataclass(frozen=True)
class DMRGConfig:
    """Configuration dataclass for DMRG calculations.

    Args:
        ncas (int):
            Number of active orbitals for the DMRG calculation.
        nelecas (int or tuple[int, int]):
            Number of active electrons, either as a total count or an explicit
            ``(nalpha, nbeta)`` pair (same convention as PySCF's CASCI).
        max_bond_dim (int, default 500):
            Target DMRG bond dimension (must be a positive multiple of 4).
            The sweep schedule starts at ``max_bond_dim // 2`` and ramps up to ``max_bond_dim``.
        symm_type ({'SZ', 'SU2'}, default 'SZ'):
            Spin symmetry used by block2. Both give spin-summed single-orbital
            entropies directly from the ``1pdm``/``1npc`` output; ``'SU2'`` is
            spin-adapted and faster. ``'SZ'`` is required only for
            ``spin_soe='resolved'`` and for unrestricted (UHF) integrals.
        verbosity (int, default 0):
            Verbosity level for block2 output.  Higher values produce more detailed logs.
        unrestricted (bool or None, default None):
            Whether to emit an unrestricted (UHF) FCIDUMP. ``None`` autodetects from
            the mean-field type (``isinstance(mf, scf.uhf.UHF)``); pass ``True``/
            ``False`` to override. UHF requires ``symm_type='SZ'``.
        reorder ({'noreorder', 'fiedler'}, default 'noreorder'):
            Orbital ordering for block2main. ``'noreorder'`` keeps the FCIDUMP order
            and enables ``full_fci_space``; ``'fiedler'`` reorders by the Fiedler
            vector and disables ``full_fci_space``.
        spin_soe ({'auto', 'summed', 'resolved'}, default 'auto'):
            Whether single-orbital entropies (and the selection built on them) are
            spin-summed or spin-resolved. ``'summed'`` uses the 4-state spatial
            entropy, so both spin channels share one entropy window; for a UHF
            reference the AO projection still returns a split ``{'alpha', 'beta'}``
            active space. ``'resolved'`` uses the
            per-spin-orbital entropies ``H(n_alpha)`` / ``H(n_beta)`` and screens the
            alpha and beta channels independently, yielding a split
            ``{'alpha', 'beta'}`` active space. ``'auto'`` picks ``'resolved'`` when
            the target is spin-polarised (``nalpha != nbeta``) and ``symm_type='SZ'``,
            else ``'summed'``. ``'resolved'`` requires ``symm_type='SZ'`` (the
            spin-resolved 1-PDM is only available without spin adaptation).
    """

    ncas: int
    nelecas: int | tuple[int, int]
    max_bond_dim: int = 500
    symm_type: Literal["SZ", "SU2"] = "SZ"
    verbosity: int = 0
    unrestricted: bool | None = None
    reorder: Literal["noreorder", "fiedler"] = "noreorder"
    spin_soe: Literal["auto", "summed", "resolved"] = "auto"

    def __post_init__(self) -> None:
        """Validate the configuration parameters.

        Raises:
            ValueError: If any of the parameters are out of their expected ranges or have invalid values.
        """
        self._validate_cas()
        self._validate_solver()

    def _validate_cas(self) -> None:
        """Validate the active-space size and electron count."""
        if self.ncas <= 0:
            raise ValueError(
                f"DMRGConfig: Number of active orbitals (`ncas`) must be positive, got {self.ncas}."
            )
        if isinstance(self.nelecas, tuple) and len(self.nelecas) != 2:
            raise ValueError(
                "DMRGConfig: `nelecas` tuple must have exactly two elements (nalpha, nbeta)."
            )
        if isinstance(self.nelecas, int) and self.nelecas <= 0:
            raise ValueError(
                f"DMRGConfig: Number of active electrons (`nelecas`) must be positive, got {self.nelecas}."
            )
        nalpha, nbeta = resolve_nelecas(self.nelecas)
        if nalpha < nbeta or nbeta < 0:
            raise ValueError(
                f"DMRGConfig: `nelecas` must satisfy nalpha >= nbeta >= 0, got {self.nelecas}."
            )

    def _validate_solver(self) -> None:
        """Validate the bond dimension, symmetry, verbosity, and ordering options."""
        if self.max_bond_dim <= 0:
            raise ValueError(
                f"DMRGConfig: Target bond dimension (`max_bond_dim`) must be positive, got {self.max_bond_dim}."
            )
        if self.max_bond_dim % 4 != 0:
            raise ValueError(
                f"DMRGConfig: `max_bond_dim` must be a multiple of 4, got {self.max_bond_dim}."
            )
        if self.symm_type not in ("SZ", "SU2"):
            raise ValueError(
                f"DMRGConfig: Invalid symmetry type (`symm_type`) {self.symm_type!r}. Must be 'SZ' or 'SU2'."
            )
        if self.verbosity < 0:
            raise ValueError(
                f"DMRGConfig: `verbosity` must be non-negative, got {self.verbosity}."
            )
        if self.reorder not in ("noreorder", "fiedler"):
            raise ValueError(
                f"DMRGConfig: Invalid reorder {self.reorder!r}. "
                "Must be 'noreorder' or 'fiedler'."
            )
        if self.unrestricted is True and self.symm_type != "SZ":
            raise ValueError(
                "DMRGConfig: `unrestricted=True` requires `symm_type='SZ'`, "
                f"got {self.symm_type!r}."
            )
        if self.spin_soe not in ("auto", "summed", "resolved"):
            raise ValueError(
                f"DMRGConfig: Invalid spin_soe {self.spin_soe!r}. "
                "Must be 'auto', 'summed', or 'resolved'."
            )
        if self.spin_soe == "resolved" and self.symm_type != "SZ":
            raise ValueError(
                "DMRGConfig: `spin_soe='resolved'` requires `symm_type='SZ'`, "
                f"got {self.symm_type!r} (the spin-resolved 1-PDM is only "
                "available without spin adaptation)."
            )

    def spin_resolved(self) -> bool:
        """Resolve *spin_soe* to a concrete spin-resolved / spin-summed choice.

        ``'auto'`` selects spin-resolved only for a spin-polarised target
        (``nalpha != nbeta``) computed with ``symm_type='SZ'``; otherwise the
        spin-summed spatial entropy is used.

        Returns:
            spin_resolved (bool): ``True`` if the single-orbital entropies
                should be spin-resolved.
        """
        if self.spin_soe == "resolved":
            return True
        if self.spin_soe == "summed":
            return False
        nalpha, nbeta = resolve_nelecas(self.nelecas)
        return nalpha != nbeta and self.symm_type == "SZ"

How to rank orbitals for entropy screening. @dataclass(frozen=True)
class EntropyConfig:
    """Configuration dataclass for entropy-based active space screening.

    Args:
        fraction (float, default 0.1):
            Entropy threshold value (see *fraction_type*).
        fraction_type ({'r', 'a'}, default 'r'):
            ``'r'``: keep orbitals whose S(1) >= ``fraction x max(S(1))``;
            ``'a'``: keep orbitals whose S(1) ≥ ``fraction`` (absolute).
        ranking ({'global', 'subset'}, default 'global'):
            How to rank orbitals for entropy screening.
            ``'global'`` ranks all active orbitals together, so a relative threshold is a
            fraction of the largest S(1) in the whole window, as in the AEGISS paper;
            ``'subset'`` applies the threshold independently to the occupied and virtual
            subspaces, each normalised by its own maximum.
    """

    fraction: float = 0.1
    fraction_type: Literal["r", "a"] = "r"
    ranking: Literal["global", "subset"] = "global"

    def __post_init__(self) -> None:
        """Validate the configuration parameters.

        Raises:
            ValueError: If any of the parameters are out of their expected ranges or have invalid values.
        """
        if not isinstance(self.fraction, (int, float)):
            raise ValueError(  # noqa: TRY004 -- documented as ValueError
                f"EntropyConfig: `fraction` must be a number, got {type(self.fraction).__name__}."
            )

        if self.fraction < 0 and self.fraction_type == "a":
            raise ValueError(
                f"EntropyConfig: `fraction` must be non-negative when `fraction_type` is 'a', got {self.fraction}."
            )
        if self.fraction_type not in ("r", "a"):
            raise ValueError(
                f"EntropyConfig: Invalid `fraction_type` {self.fraction_type!r}. Must be 'r' or 'a'."
            )
        if not (0 <= self.fraction <= 1) and self.fraction_type == "r":
            raise ValueError(
                f"EntropyConfig: `fraction` must be in the range [0, 1], got {self.fraction}."
            )
        if self.ranking not in ("subset", "global"):
            raise ValueError(
                f"EntropyConfig: Invalid `ranking` {self.ranking!r}. Must be 'subset' or 'global'."
            )

@dataclass(frozen=True)
class ProjectionConfig:
    """Configuration dataclass for orbital selection based on atomic orbital projection.

    Args:
        ao_labels (list[str | list[str]]):
            AO labels to project onto. Each entry is either a single label string
            (e.g. ``"Fe 3d"``) or a list of strings treated as one group
            (e.g. ``["Fe 3d", "Fe 4d"]``).
        basis (str or None, default 'minao'):
            Basis set used for AO projection.  ``None`` uses the original
            molecular basis.
        contribution (float or list[float], default 0.5):
            Projection weight threshold (see *contribution_type*). A list specifies
            per-label thresholds and must be non-empty; if its length does not match
            *ao_labels*, the first value is broadcast to all labels.
        contribution_type ({'a', 'r'}, default 'a'):
            ``'a'``: absolute threshold;
            ``'r'``: relative to the maximum weight.
        top_n (int | list[int] |  None, default None):
            If set, keep the top-N orbitals per AO label instead of using a
            contribution threshold. If a list is provided, it must be non-empty and either
            match the length of *ao_labels* or be broadcastable to it.
        ranking ({'subset', 'global'}, default 'subset'):
            ``'subset'``: run AO projection independently on the occupied and virtual entropy-screened subspaces;
            ``'global'``: run it on the combined set.
    """

    ao_labels: list[str | list[str]]
    basis: str | None = "minao"
    contribution: float | list[float] = 0.5
    contribution_type: Literal["a", "r"] = "a"
    top_n: int | list[int] | None = None
    ranking: Literal["subset", "global"] = "subset"

    def __post_init__(self) -> None:
        """Validate the configuration parameters.

        Raises:
            ValueError: If any of the parameters are out of their expected ranges or have invalid values.
        """
        if not isinstance(self.ao_labels, list):
            raise ValueError(  # noqa: TRY004 -- documented as ValueError
                "ProjectionConfig: `ao_labels` must be a non-empty list."
            )
        if len(self.ao_labels) == 0:
            raise ValueError("ProjectionConfig: `ao_labels` must be a non-empty list.")

        if not (
            isinstance(self.ao_labels, list)
            and self.ao_labels
            and all(_valid_ao_label(label) for label in self.ao_labels)
        ):
            raise ValueError(
                "ProjectionConfig: `ao_labels` must be a non-empty list where each "
                "entry is a non-empty string or a non-empty list of strings."
            )
        if self.contribution_type not in ("a", "r"):
            raise ValueError(
                "ProjectionConfig: Invalid `contribution_type` "
                f"{self.contribution_type!r}. Must be 'a' or 'r'."
            )
        if self.ranking not in ("subset", "global"):
            raise ValueError(
                f"ProjectionConfig: Invalid `ranking` {self.ranking!r}. Must be 'subset' or 'global'."
            )

        _helper_contributions(self.contribution, self.contribution_type)

        if self.top_n is not None:
            _helper_top_n(top_n=self.top_n)

def build_mol(atom: Any, **kwargs: Any) -> Any:
    """Helper function to build a PySCF molecule object.

    Args:
        atom (str or list of str): Atomic geometry in PySCF format, e.g. ``"N 0 0 0; N 0 0 1.1"`` or
            ``["N 0 0 0", "N 0 0 1.1"]``.
        **kwargs: Additional keyword arguments to pass to the Mole object,
            e.g. ``basis="ccpvdz"``.

    Returns:
        mol (pyscf.gto.Mole): Molecule object with specified geometry and basis set.
    """
    logger.info("----------Building Molecule----------")
    mol = scf.gto.Mole()
    mol.atom = atom
    if "max_memory" not in kwargs:
        mol.max_memory = pyscf_max_memory()
    logger.info("Molecular geometry:")
    logger.info("%s", mol.atom)
    for key, val in kwargs.items():
        logger.debug("Setting mol.%s = %s", key, val)
        setattr(mol, key, val)
    mol.build()
    return mol

def run_scf(
    mol: Any,
    method: str = "RHF",
    xc: str = "b3lyp",
    solvent_info: tuple[str, float] | None = None,
    relativistic: str | None = None,
    **kwargs: Any,
) -> Any:
    """Run an HF or KS-DFT mean-field calculation.

    Args:
        mol (pyscf.gto.Mole): Molecular geometry and basis set.
        method ({'RHF', 'UHF', 'RKS', 'UKS'}, optional): Level of theory. Default is ``'RHF'``.
        xc (str, optional): Exchange-correlation functional; only used when *method* is
            ``'RKS'`` or ``'UKS'``. Default is ``'b3lyp'``.
        solvent_info (tuple[str, float], optional): Solvent model to use, specified as
            ``(model, dielectric_constant)``, e.g. ``('IEF-PCM', 78.4)`` for water.
            *model* is case-insensitive. ``'C-PCM'`` / ``'CPCM'`` and
            ``'IEF-PCM'`` / ``'IEFPCM'`` select PySCF's PCM solver with that
            variant; ``'DDCOSMO'`` selects ddCOSMO. Any other name containing
            ``'PCM'`` (including plain ``'PCM'``) makes PySCF raise
            ``RuntimeError`` when the SCF runs; any name containing neither
            ``'PCM'`` nor ``'DDCOSMO'`` (e.g. ``'COSMO'``) is silently ignored
            and the calculation runs without solvent. Default is ``None`` (no
            solvent).
        relativistic ({'x2c'} or None, optional): Relativistic correction to apply.
            ``'x2c'`` applies the scalar exact two-component (X2C) transformation via
            ``mf.x2c()``. Default is ``None`` (no relativistic correction).
        **kwargs: Additional attributes forwarded to the PySCF mean-field object
            (e.g. ``max_cycle=50``).

    Returns:
        mf (pyscf.scf.SCF or pyscf.dft.KohnShamDFT): Converged mean-field object.

    Raises:
        ValueError: If *method* is not one of ``'RHF'``, ``'UHF'``, ``'RKS'``,
            ``'UKS'``, or if *relativistic* is empty or not ``'x2c'``.
        RuntimeError: Raised by PySCF if *solvent_info* names an unsupported
            PCM variant (see *solvent_info*).
    """
    method = method.upper()

    logger.info("----------SCF Calculation (Method %s)----------", method)

    if method in ("RHF", "UHF"):
        mf = getattr(scf, method)(mol)
    elif method in ("RKS", "UKS"):
        mf = getattr(dft, method)(mol)
        mf.xc = xc
    else:
        raise ValueError(f"Unknown method '{method}'. Choose from RHF, UHF, RKS, UKS.")

    for key, val in kwargs.items():
        setattr(mf, key, val)

    if solvent_info is not None:
        from pyscf.solvent import DDCOSMO, PCM  # noqa: PLC0415, F401

        model, eps = solvent_info
        model = model.upper()
        if "PCM" in model:
            mf = mf.PCM()
            mf.with_solvent.method = model
            mf.with_solvent.eps = eps
        elif "DDCOSMO" in model:
            mf = mf.DDCOSMO()
            mf.with_solvent.method = model
            mf.with_solvent.eps = eps

    if relativistic is not None:
        relativistic = relativistic.strip().lower()
        if not relativistic:
            raise ValueError("Relativistic method must be specified. Choose from: x2c.")
        if relativistic == "x2c":
            logger.info("Applying X2C scalar relativistic correction.")
            mf = mf.x2c()
        else:
            raise ValueError(
                f"Unknown relativistic method '{relativistic}'. Choose from: x2c."
            )

    mf.kernel()
    _log_scf_result(mf, method)
    return mf

docs.title: Localization
docs.text:
Orbital localization methods. localize is a dispatcher that accepts a method name as its first argument; each specific function can also be called directly.

from aegiss.localization import localize

Localized orbitals and the DMRG window

The DMRG active region is a window of ncas orbitals taken by index around the occupied/virtual boundary. For canonical orbitals that is a Fermi-level window, because their index order follows the orbital energies. Localization rotates the occupied and virtual blocks separately: the occupied/virtual partition survives, but localized orbitals have no orbital energies and their order within each block is arbitrary, so the same index window no longer selects the frontier orbitals. Natural orbitals are ordered by occupation number, a different but meaningful criterion. Localized orbitals can still be used, but check that the window contains the orbitals you care about. See Methodology.

    Args:
        method (str):
            One of ``'boys'``, ``'edmiston'`` / ``'er'``, ``'pm'`` / ``'pipek'``,
            ``'ibos'`` / ``'ibo'``, ``'iaos'`` / ``'iao'``, ``'nos'``, ``'fnos'``.
        *args:
            Positional arguments forwarded to the selected method.
        **kwargs:
            Keyword arguments forwarded to the selected method.

    Raises:
        ValueError: If *method* is not one of the names listed above.

    Note:
        Localized orbitals have no orbital energies, so the index-based DMRG window
        (``ncas`` orbitals around the occupied/virtual boundary) is no longer a
        Fermi-level window when built on them.

    Example:
        >>> localize("pm", mol, mf, on_virtual=True)
        >>> localize("ibos", mol, mf)
        >>> localize("iaos", mol, mf, minao="minao")
        >>> localize("nos", mf, correlated_method="mp2")
        >>> localize("fnos", mf, correlated_method="mp2", frozen=[0])
        >>> localize("boys", mol, mf, n_occ=5, on_virtual=False)
    """
    if method not in _METHODS:
        raise ValueError(
            f"Unknown localization method {method!r}. Choose from: {sorted(_METHODS)}"
        )
    return _METHODS[method](*args, **kwargs)

Intrinsic Bond Orbital (IBO) localization.

Localizes occupied MOs by maximising their population on intrinsic atomic orbitals (IAOs). IBOs tend to give chemically intuitive bond and lone-pair orbitals, and handle systems with mixed ionic/covalent character well.

Parameters:

Name Type Description Default mol Mole

Molecular geometry and basis set.

required mf SCF

Converged mean-field object supplying mo_coeff and mo_occ.

required n_occ int

Number of occupied orbitals. Inferred from mf if not given.

None minao str

Reference minimal basis used for IAO construction (default "minao").

'minao' exponent int

Exponent in the IBO localization criterion (default 4).

4

Name Type Description new_mos (ndarray, shape(nao, nmo))

IBO coefficients for the occupied block; virtual block is unchanged.

def localize_ibos(
    mol: gto.Mole,
    mf: Any,
    n_occ: int | None = None,
    *,
    minao: str = "minao",
    exponent: int = 4,
) -> np.ndarray:
    """Intrinsic Bond Orbital (IBO) localization.

    Localizes occupied MOs by maximising their population on intrinsic atomic
    orbitals (IAOs). IBOs tend to give chemically intuitive bond and lone-pair
    orbitals, and handle systems with mixed ionic/covalent character well.

    Args:
        mol (pyscf.gto.Mole):
            Molecular geometry and basis set.
        mf (pyscf.scf.hf.SCF):
            Converged mean-field object supplying ``mo_coeff`` and ``mo_occ``.
        n_occ (int, optional):
            Number of occupied orbitals. Inferred from *mf* if not given.
        minao (str):
            Reference minimal basis used for IAO construction (default ``"minao"``).
        exponent (int):
            Exponent in the IBO localization criterion (default ``4``).

    Returns:
        new_mos (np.ndarray, shape (nao, nmo)):
            IBO coefficients for the occupied block; virtual block is unchanged.
    """
    from pyscf.lo import ibo as _ibo  # noqa: PLC0415

    if mol.natm == 1:
        logger.warning(
            "IBO localization skipped: single-atom molecule has no bonds to localize."
        )
        return np.array(mf.mo_coeff)
    if n_occ is None:
        n_occ = int(np.count_nonzero(mf.mo_occ > 0))
    loc_occ = _ibo.ibo(mol, mf.mo_coeff[:, :n_occ], minao=minao, exponent=exponent)
    return np.hstack((loc_occ, mf.mo_coeff[:, n_occ:]))

Intrinsic Atomic Orbital (IAO) construction.

Constructs orthonormal IAOs that closely resemble minimal-basis atomic orbitals while spanning the occupied MO space. IAOs are useful as a chemically meaningful occupied basis for population analysis and as a starting point for IBO construction.

There is one IAO per function of the reference minimal basis, which is in general more than the number of occupied orbitals, so the result is a basis for the occupied space and cannot replace mf.mo_coeff.

Parameters:

Name Type Description Default mol Mole

Molecular geometry and basis set.

required mf SCF

Converged mean-field object supplying mo_coeff and mo_occ.

required n_occ int

Number of occupied orbitals. Inferred from mf if not given.

None minao str

Reference minimal basis (default "minao").

'minao'

Returns:

Name Type Description iaos (ndarray, shape(nao, n_iao))

Löwdin-orthogonalized IAO coefficients, with n_iao the size of the minao basis (n_iao >= n_occ).

Source code in src/aegiss/localization/orbital_localization.py 
def localize_iaos(
    mol: gto.Mole,
    mf: Any,
    n_occ: int | None = None,
    *,
    minao: str = "minao",
) -> np.ndarray:
    """Intrinsic Atomic Orbital (IAO) construction.

    Constructs orthonormal IAOs that closely resemble minimal-basis atomic
    orbitals while spanning the occupied MO space. IAOs are useful as a
    chemically meaningful occupied basis for population analysis and as a
    starting point for IBO construction.

    There is one IAO per function of the reference minimal basis, which is in
    general more than the number of occupied orbitals, so the result is a basis
    for the occupied space and cannot replace ``mf.mo_coeff``.

    Args:
        mol (pyscf.gto.Mole):
            Molecular geometry and basis set.
        mf (pyscf.scf.hf.SCF):
            Converged mean-field object supplying ``mo_coeff`` and ``mo_occ``.
        n_occ (int, optional):
            Number of occupied orbitals. Inferred from *mf* if not given.
        minao (str):
            Reference minimal basis (default ``"minao"``).

    Returns:
        iaos (np.ndarray, shape (nao, n_iao)):
            Löwdin-orthogonalized IAO coefficients, with ``n_iao`` the size of the
            *minao* basis (``n_iao >= n_occ``).
    """
    from pyscf.lo import iao as _iao  # noqa: PLC0415
    from pyscf.lo import orth as _orth  # noqa: PLC0415

    if n_occ is None:
        n_occ = int(np.count_nonzero(mf.mo_occ > 0))
    iaos = _iao.iao(mol, mf.mo_coeff[:, :n_occ], minao=minao)
    s = mol.intor_symmetric("int1e_ovlp")
    return np.asarray(_orth.vec_lowdin(iaos, s))

def localize_fnos(
    mf: Any,
    correlated_method: Literal["mp2", "cisd", "ccsd"],
    active: bool | list[int] = True,  # noqa: FBT001, FBT002
    *,
    frozen: list[int] | None = None,
) -> np.ndarray:
    """Frozen natural orbital (FNO) transformation.

    Builds a correlated wavefunction, partitions orbitals into a frozen core and
    an active set, and returns the FNO coefficient matrix.

    Args:
        mf (pyscf.scf.hf.SCF):
            Converged mean-field object.
        correlated_method ({'mp2', 'cisd', 'ccsd'}):
            Correlated method used to build the 1-RDM for the NO transformation.
        active (True or list of int):
            Controls which occupied orbitals enter the correlated calculation.
            ``True`` uses all occupied orbitals (no freezing). A list of integers
            specifies the indices of the active occupied orbitals; all others
            are frozen. Ignored when *frozen* is provided. Indices are given in
            the configured display base (see :func:`aegiss.utils.orb_display.orbital_base`):
            0-based by default, or 1-based when ``AEGISS_ORB_BASE=1``.
        frozen (list of int, optional):
            Indices of occupied orbitals to freeze, in the configured display
            base (0-based by default; 1-based when ``AEGISS_ORB_BASE=1``). Takes
            precedence over *active* when provided.

    Returns:
        mo_coeff (np.ndarray, shape (nao, nmo)):
            FNO coefficients in the AO basis.
    """
    from aegiss.localization.fnos import compute_fnos  # noqa: PLC0415

    logger.info("Computing FNOs using %s", correlated_method.upper())

    orbital_list: list[int]
    if frozen is not None:
        # `frozen` is user input in the display base; convert to 0-based first.
        # `frozen` names the orbitals to exclude; active for get_orbital_spaces
        # is the complement.
        frozen_set = set(from_display_all(frozen))
        orbital_list = [
            int(i) for i in np.nonzero(mf.mo_occ > 0)[0] if i not in frozen_set
        ]
    elif isinstance(active, list):
        # `active` is user input in the display base; convert to 0-based.
        orbital_list = from_display_all(active)
    elif active is True:
        orbital_list = []
    else:
        raise ValueError(
            "active=False is not supported; pass True to use all occupied orbitals or a list of active orbital indices."
        )
    frozen_orbs, active_orbs, _, frozen_virt = get_orbital_spaces(
        mf,
        orbital_list=orbital_list,
        unique_virt_space=True,
    )
    wfn_obj = build_correlated_wfn(mf, correlated_method, frozen=frozen_orbs)
    logger.info("Frozen orbitals: %s", to_display_all(frozen_orbs))
    logger.info("Active orbitals: %s", to_display_all(active_orbs))
    logger.info("Frozen virtual orbitals: %s", to_display_all(frozen_virt))

    return compute_fnos(
        wfn_obj,
        frozen=frozen_orbs.tolist(),
        active=active_orbs.tolist(),
    )

Compute natural orbitals from a correlated wavefunction object.

Extracts the 1-RDM from wfn_obj (CISD, CCSD, CASCI/CASSCF, …), diagonalises it, and returns the NOs sorted by descending occupation.

Parameters:

Name Type Description Default wfn_obj correlated PySCF solver object

Must expose a make_rdm1 method returning the 1-RDM in the MO basis.

required split_nos bool

Obtain the Natural Orbital basis by diagonalizing the 1-RDM in the occupied and virtual subspaces separately. Useful for certain post-HF methods where the occupied and virtual spaces are treated differently.

False

Returns:

Name Type Description nos (ndarray, shape(nao, nmo))

Natural orbital coefficients in the AO basis.

Source code in src/aegiss/localization/nos.py 
def compute_nos(wfn_obj: Any, *, split_nos: bool = False) -> np.ndarray:
    """Compute natural orbitals from a correlated wavefunction object.

    Extracts the 1-RDM from *wfn_obj* (CISD, CCSD, CASCI/CASSCF, …),
    diagonalises it, and returns the NOs sorted by descending occupation.

    Args:
        wfn_obj (correlated PySCF solver object):
            Must expose a ``make_rdm1`` method returning the 1-RDM in the MO basis.
        split_nos (bool, optional):
            Obtain the Natural Orbital basis by diagonalizing the 1-RDM in the
            occupied and virtual subspaces separately. Useful for certain post-HF
            methods where the occupied and virtual spaces are treated differently.

    Returns:
        nos (np.ndarray, shape (nao, nmo)):
            Natural orbital coefficients in the AO basis.
    """
    rdm1_mo = wfn_obj.make_rdm1()
    logger.debug("1-RDM in MO basis:\n%s", rdm1_mo.shape)
    if split_nos:
        logger.info(
            "Building Split NOs by diagonalizing occupied and virtual blocks separately."
        )
        nocc = wfn_obj.nocc
        rdm1_occ = rdm1_mo[:nocc, :nocc]
        rdm1_virt = rdm1_mo[nocc:, nocc:]

        occ_occ, u_occ = np.linalg.eigh(rdm1_occ)
        occ_virt, u_virt = np.linalg.eigh(rdm1_virt)

        # Sort occupied and virtual NOs separately
        idx_occ = np.argsort(occ_occ)[::-1]
        idx_virt = np.argsort(occ_virt)[::-1]

        u_occ = u_occ[:, idx_occ]
        u_virt = u_virt[:, idx_virt]

        # Combine occupied and virtual NOs back into a single MO coefficient matrix
        nos_occ = wfn_obj.mo_coeff[:, :nocc] @ u_occ
        nos_virt = wfn_obj.mo_coeff[:, nocc:] @ u_virt
        return np.hstack((nos_occ, nos_virt))
    logger.info("Building standard NOs by diagonalizing the full 1-RDM.")
    occ_mo, u = np.linalg.eigh(rdm1_mo)
    # sort descending
    idx = np.argsort(occ_mo)[::-1]
    u = u[:, idx]
    # pyscf post-HF objects expose their SCF only as `_scf`
    scf = getattr(wfn_obj, "_scf", wfn_obj)
    mo_coeff = scf.mo_coeff
    return np.asarray(mo_coeff @ u)

Only the virtual block of the 1-RDM is diagonalised; the virtual NOs are sorted by decreasing occupation. The occupied orbitals are returned unchanged and no orbital is discarded.

def compute_fnos(
    wfn_obj: Any,
    frozen: list[int],
    active: list[int],
) -> np.ndarray:
    """Construct frozen natural orbitals by rotating the virtual space into NOs.

    Only the virtual block of the 1-RDM is diagonalised; the virtual NOs are
    sorted by decreasing occupation. The occupied orbitals are returned
    unchanged and no orbital is discarded.

    Args:
        wfn_obj (correlated PySCF solver object):
            Must expose a ``make_rdm1`` method returning the 1-RDM in the MO basis.
        frozen (list of int):
            Indices of orbitals to be frozen (0-based indexing).
        active (list of int):
            Indices of orbitals to be retained in the active space (0-based indexing).

    Returns:
        mo_coeff (np.ndarray, shape (nao, nmo)):
            Unchanged occupied (frozen and active) orbitals followed by the
            virtual FNOs, in the AO basis.
    """
    rdm1 = wfn_obj.make_rdm1()

    nocc = len(frozen) + len(active)
    logger.debug("1-RDM in MO basis:\n%s", rdm1.shape)
    logger.info(
        "Diagonalizing virtual block of the 1-RDM to construct FNOs for virtual orbitals."
    )
    dm_vv = rdm1[nocc:, nocc:]
    occ_vv, u_vv = np.linalg.eigh(dm_vv)
    idx_vv = np.argsort(occ_vv)[::-1]
    occ_vv = occ_vv[idx_vv]
    u_vv = u_vv[:, idx_vv]

    mo_coeff_vv = wfn_obj.mo_coeff[:, nocc:] @ u_vv
    mo_coeff_oo = wfn_obj.mo_coeff[:, :nocc]
    return np.hstack((mo_coeff_oo, mo_coeff_vv))

If True, orbital_list only affects the occupied space: every virtual orbital is returned in frozen_virt and active_virt is empty. If False, the virtual space is partitioned into active and frozen virtuals based on orbital_list.

active_occ np.ndarray of int

def get_orbital_spaces(
    mf: Any,
    orbital_list: list[int],
    *,
    unique_virt_space: bool = False,
) -> tuple[np.ndarray, np.ndarray, np.ndarray, np.ndarray]:
    """Partition MO indices into four subspaces.

    Args:
        mf (PySCF SCF object): Converged mean-field object exposing ``mo_occ``.
        orbital_list (list of int): Orbital indices (0-based) that define the active / selected space.
            An empty list selects every orbital: no occupied orbital is frozen
            and, when *unique_virt_space* is ``False``, every virtual orbital is
            active.
        unique_virt_space (bool): If ``True``, *orbital_list* only affects the occupied space:
            every virtual orbital is returned in *frozen_virt* and *active_virt*
            is empty. If ``False``, the virtual space is partitioned into active
            and frozen virtuals based on *orbital_list*.

    Returns:
        frozen_occ (np.ndarray of int): Occupied orbitals **not** in *orbital_list* (core / frozen occupied).
        active_occ (np.ndarray of int): Occupied orbitals that **are** in *orbital_list*.
        active_virt (np.ndarray of int): Virtual orbitals that **are** in *orbital_list* (empty when
            *unique_virt_space* is ``True``).
        frozen_virt (np.ndarray of int): Virtual orbitals **not** in *orbital_list* (external / frozen virtual);
            all virtual orbitals when *unique_virt_space* is ``True``.
    """
    selected = set(orbital_list)
    if not selected:
        logger.info(
            "Empty orbital list: treating all orbitals as selected"
            " (no frozen occupied orbitals)."
        )
        selected = set(range(len(mf.mo_occ)))
    occ_mask = mf.mo_occ > 0

    all_occ = np.where(occ_mask)[0]
    all_virt = np.where(~occ_mask)[0]

    frozen_occ = np.array([i for i in all_occ if i not in selected])
    active_occ = np.array([i for i in all_occ if i in selected])

    if unique_virt_space:
        return frozen_occ, active_occ, np.array([], dtype=int), np.array(list(all_virt))

    active_virt = np.array([i for i in all_virt if i in selected])
    frozen_virt = np.array([i for i in all_virt if i not in selected])

    return frozen_occ, active_occ, active_virt, frozen_virt

If ncas exceeds the number of MOs, if nelecas does not satisfy nalpha >= nbeta >= 0, if it exceeds the total electron count, if the window does not fit above the frozen core, or, for an unrestricted reference, if the active spin nalpha - nbeta differs from the reference spin.

def get_subspaces_from_cas(
    mf: Any,
    ncas: int,
    nelecas: int | tuple[int, int],
) -> tuple[np.ndarray, np.ndarray]:
    """Split the CAS window into its occupied and virtual parts.

    The window holds the ``ncas`` orbitals directly above the closed frozen
    core. Its orbitals are split at the reference HOMO/LUMO boundary.

    Args:
        mf (PySCF SCF object): Converged mean-field object exposing ``mo_occ``.
        ncas (int): Number of active orbitals in the CAS.
        nelecas (int or tuple[int, int]): Number of active electrons, either as a total count or an explicit
            ``(nalpha, nbeta)`` pair (same convention as PySCF's CASCI).

    Returns:
        active_occ (np.ndarray of int): Orbital indices (0-based) of the CAS window that are occupied
            in the reference (``mo_occ > 0``, SOMOs included).
        active_virt (np.ndarray of int): Orbital indices (0-based) of the CAS window that are virtual
            in the reference.

    Raises:
        ValueError: If *ncas* exceeds the number of MOs, if *nelecas* does not
            satisfy ``nalpha >= nbeta >= 0``, if it exceeds the total electron
            count, if the window does not fit above the frozen core, or, for an
            unrestricted reference, if the active spin ``nalpha - nbeta``
            differs from the reference spin.
    """
    logger.info(
        "----------DMRG CAS Subspace Selection (ncas=%d, nelecas=%s)----------",
        ncas,
        nelecas,
    )
    nalpha, nbeta = resolve_nelecas(nelecas)
    mo_occ = np.asarray(mf.mo_occ)
    # Collapse spin so the logic is identical for restricted (1-D ``mo_occ``) and
    # unrestricted (2-D, shape ``(2, nmo)``) references: a per-spatial-orbital
    # occupation with values 0 / 1 / 2.
    occ_per_orb = mo_occ.sum(axis=0) if mo_occ.ndim == 2 else mo_occ
    neletot = round(float(occ_per_orb.sum()))
    # UHF ``mo_coeff`` is a tuple/array of two (nao, nmo) blocks, restricted is a
    # single (nao, nmo) array; ``shape[-1]`` is nmo in both cases.
    nmos = np.asarray(mf.mo_coeff).shape[-1]
    nact = nalpha + nbeta

    if ncas > nmos:
        msg = "Number of active orbitals cannot exceed total number of MOs."
        raise ValueError(msg)
    if nbeta < 0 or nalpha < nbeta:
        msg = "nelecas must satisfy nalpha >= nbeta >= 0."
        raise ValueError(msg)
    if nact > neletot:
        msg = "Number of active electrons cannot exceed total number of electrons."
        raise ValueError(msg)

    # For an unrestricted reference, alpha and beta are distinct orbital sets, so a
    # single active-orbital window only exists when their frozen cores coincide:
    # ncore_a = Na - nalpha == Nb - nbeta = ncore_b, i.e. the reference spin
    # polarisation must equal the requested active spin. (A *restricted* reference
    # has one orbital set, so an open-shell active target on it is always fine.)
    if mo_occ.ndim == 2:
        na_ref = round(float(mo_occ[0].sum()))
        nb_ref = round(float(mo_occ[1].sum()))
        if (na_ref - nb_ref) != (nalpha - nbeta):
            msg = (
                f"Unrestricted reference: active spin (nalpha - nbeta = "
                f"{nalpha - nbeta}) must equal the reference spin "
                f"(Na - Nb = {na_ref - nb_ref}); otherwise the alpha and beta "
                "active windows differ and no single CAS partition exists."
            )
            raise ValueError(msg)

    # The frozen core is closed: ``ncore`` doubly-occupied spatial orbitals sit
    # below the active window, placed by the *total* active electron count (this
    # matches pyscf CASCI/UCASCI). The (nalpha, nbeta) split sets the DMRG target
    # occupation, not the window position.
    ncore = (neletot - nact) // 2
    if ncore + ncas > nmos:
        msg = "Not enough virtual orbitals to accommodate the active space."
        raise ValueError(msg)

    # The occupied/virtual label reflects the *reference* occupation: any orbital
    # with occ > 0 is "occupied" (including the singly-occupied SOMOs of an
    # open-shell reference), so the split sits at the reference HOMO boundary.
    nocc = int(np.count_nonzero(occ_per_orb > 0))
    active = np.arange(ncore, ncore + ncas)
    active_occ = active[active < nocc]
    active_virt = active[active >= nocc]

    logger.info(
        "Total MOs: %d, Occupied MOs: %d, Virtual MOs: %d", nmos, nocc, nmos - nocc
    )
    logger.info("Frozen (doubly-occupied) core orbitals: %d", ncore)
    logger.info("Active occupied orbital indices: %s", to_display_all(active_occ))
    logger.info("Active virtual orbital indices: %s\n\n", to_display_all(active_virt))

    # Return values stay 0-based so downstream slicing/logic is unaffected.
    return active_occ, active_virt

def valence_occupied_orbitals(mf: Any, *, exclude_core: bool = True) -> list[int]:
    """Return the occupied MO indices, optionally excluding the chemical core.

    Convenience helper for building a ``restricted_space`` of plain orbital
    indices (see :func:`aegiss.active_space.ao_projection.select_by_ao_projection`)
    without needing entropy scores.

    Args:
        mf (PySCF SCF object): Converged mean-field object exposing ``mo_occ`` and ``mol``.
        exclude_core (bool, keyword-only): If ``True`` (default), drop the frozen chemical-core orbitals as
            defined by :func:`pyscf.data.elements.chemcore` (1s for first-row
            atoms, 1s2s2p for second-row, and so on). The core is assumed to
            occupy the lowest ``ncore`` orbital indices, following PySCF's
            frozen-core convention; this holds for canonical SCF orbitals but
            not necessarily for localized orbitals.

    Returns:
        orbitals (list of int): Occupied orbital indices (0-based), sorted ascending.
    """
    occ = np.where(mf.mo_occ > 0)[0]
    if not exclude_core:
        return [int(i) for i in occ]
    ncore = chemcore(mf.mol)
    valence = occ[occ >= ncore]
    logger.info(
        "Excluding %d chemical-core orbital(s); %d valence occupied orbital(s) remain.",
        ncore,
        len(valence),
    )
    return [int(i) for i in valence]

def resolve_nelecas(nelecas: int | tuple[int, int]) -> tuple[int, int]:
    """Normalise *nelecas* to an (nalpha, nbeta) pair.

    Args:
        nelecas (int or tuple[int, int]): Either a total electron count (PySCF closed-shell convention) or an
            explicit ``(nalpha, nbeta)`` pair.  Odd integers are treated as
            high-spin doublets (nalpha = ceil, nbeta = floor).

    Returns:
        nalpha, nbeta (tuple[int, int]):
    """
    if isinstance(nelecas, tuple):
        return nelecas
    return (nelecas + 1) // 2, nelecas // 2

def combine_candidate_entropies(
    occ_orbs: list[tuple[int, float]], virt_orbs: list[tuple[int, float]]
) -> list[tuple[int, float]]:
    """Merge and sort occupied and virtual orbital candidate lists.

    Args:
        occ_orbs (list of tuple[int, float]): Occupied orbital index/entropy pairs.
        virt_orbs (list of tuple[int, float]): Virtual orbital index/entropy pairs.

    Returns:
        combined_space (list of tuple[int, float]): Merged list sorted by orbital index.
    """
    combined_space = occ_orbs + virt_orbs
    combined_space.sort(key=lambda x: x[0])
    return combined_space

def orbital_base() -> int:
    """Return the configured display base for orbital indices (``0`` or ``1``).

    Applies the precedence documented in the module docstring: environment
    variable, then config file, then the default of ``0``. The result is cached
    for the lifetime of the process; call :func:`reset_cache` after mutating the
    environment or config file (e.g. in tests).

    """
    for resolver in (_base_from_env, _base_from_config):
        base = resolver()
        if base is not None:
            return base
    return _DEFAULT_BASE

def from_display(index: int) -> int:
    """Convert a user-supplied *index* (in the display base) to 0-based storage.

    Args:
        index (int): An orbital index as typed by the user, in the display base.

    Returns:
        int: The equivalent 0-based index for internal use.
    """
    base = orbital_base()
    idx = int(index)
    if idx < base:
        raise ValueError(
            f"Orbital index {idx} is invalid for base {base} (expected >= {base})."
        )
    return idx - base

def from_display_all(indices: Iterable[int]) -> list[int]:
    """Vectorised :func:`from_display` for user-supplied indices.

    Args:
        indices (Iterable[int]): Orbital indices as typed by the user, in the
            display base.

    Returns:
        list[int]: The equivalent 0-based indices for internal use.
    """
    base = orbital_base()
    raw = [int(i) for i in indices]
    bad = [i for i in raw if i < base]
    if bad:
        raise ValueError(
            f"Orbital indices {bad} are invalid for base {base} (expected >= {base})."
        )
    return [i - base for i in raw]

def save_orbitals(
    mol: Any,
    mo_coeff: np.ndarray,
    candidate_indices: np.ndarray,
    filename_prefix: str = "mo",
    folder: str = "./",
) -> None:
    """Save molecular orbitals as cube files for visualization.

    Args:
        mol (pyscf.gto.Mole): Molecule object containing the geometry and basis set information.
        mo_coeff (np.ndarray): Molecular orbital coefficients in the AO basis. Shape (n_ao, n_mo).
        candidate_indices (np.ndarray): Indices of the orbitals to save.
        filename_prefix (str): Prefix for the output cube files. Each orbital is saved as
            ``"{filename_prefix}_{i}.cube"``, where ``i`` is the orbital index
            in the configured display base (see
            :func:`aegiss.utils.orb_display.to_display`).
        folder (str): Output directory path. Created if it does not exist.
    """
    from pyscf.tools import cubegen  # noqa: PLC0415

    output_dir = Path(folder)
    output_dir.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)

    for i in candidate_indices:
        # File name carries the display-base index; slicing stays 0-based.
        filename = output_dir / f"{filename_prefix}_{to_display(i)}.cube"
        cubegen.orbital(mol, str(filename), mo_coeff[:, i])

docs.title: Entropy and mutual information
docs.text:
The AEGISS pipeline computes single-orbital entropies only: select_aegiss and run_dmrg_subprocess do not return an orbital mutual-information (MI) matrix. The MI plots (mi_plot and entanglement_diagrams) and dump_qmi therefore take a matrix computed elsewhere, for example with block2's Python API, where DMRGDriver.get_orbital_interaction_matrix(ket) returns \(I_{ij} = \tfrac{1}{2}(S_i + S_j - S_{ij})\) with a zero diagonal, or with any other DMRG or CI code.

import numpy as np

from aegiss.utils.dump import dump_qmi
from aegiss.utils.plotting import entanglement_diagrams, mi_plot

window = [16, 19, 20, 21, 22, 29]           # 0-based MO indices of the orbitals
s1 = np.array([0.31, 0.52, 0.55, 0.54, 0.51, 0.30])  # S(1) per orbital (illustrative)
minfo = np.load("benzene_mi.npy")           # (6, 6) MI matrix in the same order

soe1 = list(zip(window, s1))                # (orbital_index, S1) pairs
mi_plot(minfo, soe1, folder="plots", filename="benzene_MI")
entanglement_diagrams(soe1, minfo, folder="plots", filename="benzene_entanglement")
dump_qmi(minfo, s1, path="plots/benzene_qmi.npz")

What the external matrix must satisfy:

  • It is a symmetric (n, n) array whose row and column k belong to the orbital soe1[k][0], the same orbitals (same mo_coeff) that the entropies refer to. If the external calculation reorders the orbitals, for example with a Fiedler ordering, map the matrix back to your orbital order first.
  • entanglement_diagrams reads only the upper triangle and normalises by the largest value, so the overall scale and the MI convention (with or without the factor 1/2) do not change the diagram.
  • mi_plot draws the whole matrix on a 0 to max colour scale, so set the diagonal to zero.
  • The single-orbital entropies can come from AEGISS itself: run_dmrg_subprocess returns them for the window from get_subspaces_from_cas, ordered occupied first, then virtual.

    The arrays are stored under the keys ``"minfo"``, ``"soe1"`` and ``"soe2"``
    and can be read back with ``np.load``. The AEGISS pipeline does not compute
    mutual information, so *minfo* comes from an external calculation (see
    :func:`aegiss.utils.plotting.mi_plot`).

    Args:
        minfo (np.ndarray): Mutual information matrix.
        soe1 (np.ndarray): Single orbital entropy values.
        soe2 (np.ndarray or None): Double orbital entropy values, or ``None`` if not computed.
        path (Path or str): Output file path. numpy appends ``.npz`` when the
            path does not already end with it.
    """
    filename = Path(path)
    data: dict[str, np.ndarray] = {"minfo": minfo, "soe1": soe1}
    if soe2 is not None:
        data["soe2"] = soe2
    np.savez(filename, **data)  # ty: ignore[invalid-argument-type]
    logger.info("QMI data dumped to %s", filename)

docs.title: mo_ao_contributions(mf: Any, mo_indices: int | Sequence[int], *, top_n: int = 10, group_by_element: bool = False, clusters: Mapping[int, Sequence[int]] | None = None) -> dict[int, dict[str, list[tuple[int, str, float]]]]
docs.text:
Log and return the top-N atomic-orbital contributions to one or more MOs.

For each requested molecular orbital the AO basis functions are ranked by the magnitude of their expansion coefficient mo_coeff[mu, i] and the top_n largest are kept. The signed coefficient is reported, so the orbital's phase is preserved. Useful for inspecting an MO that shows only a small weight in an AO-projection heatmap: it reveals which AOs the orbital is actually built from.

When group_by_element is set, contributions are instead collapsed by element symbol and basis label (the atom index is dropped), so every C 2pz across the molecule is merged into one "C 2pz" group whose weight is the sum of the absolute coefficients of its members. Groups are ranked by that summed magnitude.

When clusters is given, contributions are collapsed by cluster and basis label instead: each atom is mapped to the cluster containing it (atoms in no cluster fall into a catch-all group keyed U), and |coefficient| is summed over all atoms of a cluster sharing a basis label. The group label reads "(<cluster id>) <elements> <ao_label>", e.g. "(0) C 2pz" (or "(U) H 1s" for unassigned atoms). The cluster membership — each cluster's atoms with indices — is logged first. clusters and group_by_element are mutually exclusive.

The result is always logged as a table with one column per orbital (restricted) or a pair of alpha/beta columns per orbital (unrestricted).

Parameters:

Name Type Description Default mf SCF

Converged mean-field object exposing mo_coeff and mol. mo_coeff may be restricted (n_ao, n_mo) or unrestricted (2, n_ao, n_mo); in the latter case both spins are reported.

required mo_indices int or sequence of int

Index (or indices) of the molecular orbital(s) to decompose, in the configured display base (0-based by default; 1-based when AEGISS_ORB_BASE=1). Returned dict keys are always 0-based.

required top_n int

Number of largest AO contributions (or element groups) to keep per orbital.

10 group_by_element bool

If True, sum |coefficient| over all atoms of the same element sharing a basis label, ranking the resulting groups instead of individual AOs.

False clusters mapping of int to sequence of int

Maps a cluster id to the atom indices it contains. Atom indices are always 0-based (PySCF atom order), regardless of the orbital display base. When given, sum |coefficient| over the atoms of each cluster sharing a basis label. Atoms must each belong to at most one cluster; any not listed fall into the catch-all U group. Mutually exclusive with group_by_element.

None

Returns:

Name Type Description composition dict[int, dict[str, list[tuple[int, str, float]]]]

Maps each requested MO index to a {spin: entries} dict, where spin is "alpha" (and "beta" for unrestricted inputs) and entries is a list of (key, label, weight) triples ordered from largest to smallest weight. Ungrouped: key is the AO index, label the PySCF AO label and weight the signed coefficient. Grouped (by element or cluster): key is the number of AOs in the group and weight the summed |coefficient|.

Source code in src/aegiss/utils/mo_composition.py 
def mo_ao_contributions(
    mf: Any,
    mo_indices: int | Sequence[int],
    *,
    top_n: int = 10,
    group_by_element: bool = False,
    clusters: Mapping[int, Sequence[int]] | None = None,
) -> dict[int, dict[str, list[tuple[int, str, float]]]]:
    """Log and return the top-N atomic-orbital contributions to one or more MOs.

    For each requested molecular orbital the AO basis functions are ranked by
    the magnitude of their expansion coefficient ``mo_coeff[mu, i]`` and the
    *top_n* largest are kept. The signed coefficient is reported, so the
    orbital's phase is preserved. Useful for inspecting an MO that shows only a
    small weight in an AO-projection heatmap: it reveals which AOs the orbital
    is actually built from.

    When *group_by_element* is set, contributions are instead collapsed by
    element symbol and basis label (the atom index is dropped), so every
    ``C 2pz`` across the molecule is merged into one ``"C 2pz"`` group whose
    weight is the sum of the absolute coefficients of its members. Groups are
    ranked by that summed magnitude.

    When *clusters* is given, contributions are collapsed by cluster and basis
    label instead: each atom is mapped to the cluster containing it (atoms in no
    cluster fall into a catch-all group keyed ``U``), and ``|coefficient|`` is
    summed over all atoms of a cluster sharing a basis label. The group label
    reads ``"(<cluster id>) <elements> <ao_label>"``, e.g. ``"(0) C 2pz"`` (or
    ``"(U) H 1s"`` for unassigned atoms). The cluster membership — each cluster's
    atoms with indices — is logged first. *clusters* and *group_by_element* are
    mutually exclusive.

    The result is always logged as a table with one column per orbital
    (restricted) or a pair of alpha/beta columns per orbital (unrestricted).

    Args:
        mf (pyscf.scf.hf.SCF): Converged mean-field object exposing ``mo_coeff``
            and ``mol``. ``mo_coeff`` may be restricted ``(n_ao, n_mo)`` or
            unrestricted ``(2, n_ao, n_mo)``; in the latter case both spins are
            reported.
        mo_indices (int or sequence of int): Index (or indices) of the molecular
            orbital(s) to decompose, in the configured display base (0-based by
            default; 1-based when ``AEGISS_ORB_BASE=1``). Returned dict keys are
            always 0-based.
        top_n (int): Number of largest AO contributions (or element groups) to
            keep per orbital.
        group_by_element (bool): If ``True``, sum ``|coefficient|`` over all
            atoms of the same element sharing a basis label, ranking the
            resulting groups instead of individual AOs.
        clusters (mapping of int to sequence of int, optional): Maps a cluster id
            to the atom indices it contains. Atom indices are always 0-based
            (PySCF atom order), regardless of the orbital display base. When
            given, sum ``|coefficient|``
            over the atoms of each cluster sharing a basis label. Atoms must each
            belong to at most one cluster; any not listed fall into the catch-all
            ``U`` group. Mutually exclusive with *group_by_element*.

    Returns:
        composition (dict[int, dict[str, list[tuple[int, str, float]]]]): Maps
            each requested MO index to a ``{spin: entries}`` dict, where *spin*
            is ``"alpha"`` (and ``"beta"`` for unrestricted inputs) and *entries*
            is a list of ``(key, label, weight)`` triples ordered from largest to
            smallest weight. Ungrouped: ``key`` is the AO index, *label* the
            PySCF AO label and ``weight`` the signed coefficient. Grouped (by
            element or cluster): ``key`` is the number of AOs in the group and
            ``weight`` the summed ``|coefficient|``.
    """
    if clusters is not None and group_by_element:
        raise ValueError("Pass at most one of `group_by_element` and `clusters`.")

    # `mo_indices` is user input in the display base; convert to 0-based storage.
    indices = from_display_all(
        [mo_indices] if isinstance(mo_indices, int) else mo_indices
    )

    mo_coeff = mf.mo_coeff
    unrestricted = np.ndim(mo_coeff) == 3
    channels = (
        (("alpha", mo_coeff[0]), ("beta", mo_coeff[1]))
        if unrestricted
        else (("alpha", mo_coeff),)
    )
    ao_labels = mf.mol.ao_labels()
    grouped = group_by_element or clusters is not None
    ao_struct = mf.mol.ao_labels(fmt=False) if grouped else None
    n_mo = channels[0][1].shape[1]

    if clusters is not None:
        _validate_clusters(clusters, mf.mol.natm)
        _log_cluster_membership(mf.mol, clusters)

    composition: dict[int, dict[str, list[tuple[int, str, float]]]] = {}
    for mo_idx in indices:
        if not 0 <= mo_idx < n_mo:
            raise ValueError(
                f"MO index {to_display(mo_idx)} out of range "
                f"[{to_display(0)}, {to_display(n_mo)})."
            )
        per_spin = {
            spin: _entries_for_coeff(
                coeff_matrix[:, mo_idx],
                top_n,
                ao_labels=ao_labels,
                ao_struct=ao_struct,
                clusters=clusters,
            )
            for spin, coeff_matrix in channels
        }
        composition[mo_idx] = per_spin

    if clusters is not None:
        detail = "summed |mo_coeff| per cluster+label"
    elif group_by_element:
        detail = "summed |mo_coeff| per element+label"
    else:
        detail = "signed mo_coeff entries"
    logger.info(
        "Top-%d AO contributions per MO (%s):\n%s",
        top_n,
        detail,
        _format_composition_table(composition, top_n, unrestricted=unrestricted),
    )
    return composition

docs.text:
The examples below are produced by docs/scripts/generate_doc_plots.py from a real benzene calculation (RHF/cc-pVDZ, a DMRG in the frontier CAS(30,30), and an AO projection onto the minao reference). Re-run that script to refresh them.

Example — single-orbital entropies \(S(1)_i\) across the benzene frontier CAS(30,30). The top row shows each orbital's entropy; the lower rows mark which survive the threshold \(\tau_E\) and which are left empty. The entanglement concentrates on the π-type frontier orbitals (around 19–22), with most of the 30 CAS orbitals nearly inactive.

Example — the number of retained orbitals as the entropy threshold is swept from 0 to \(S(1)_{\max}\). Two plateaus emerge — a broad CAS(6,6) at intermediate thresholds and a stable CAS(4,4) at higher ones — the latter being the benzene π active space.

Example — projection weight of each frontier MO onto three AO manifolds (C 2pz, C 2s, H 1s). The π orbitals (19–22) light up in the C 2pz row, while the σ framework spreads over C 2s/H 1s.

Example — per-orbital composition of the benzene valence σ orbitals, showing how each mixes C 2s, C 2px, C 2py and H 1s character.

docs.title: soe_heatmap(so1_entropies: list[tuple[int, float]], n_occ: int = 0, folder: str = './', filename: str = 'SOE_plot', fmt: str | None = 'pdf') -> None
docs.text:
Plot a single-orbital entropy (SOE) heatmap.

Displays a 5-row matrix where the top three rows show the absolute S(1) values on a fixed [0, 1] colormap, and the bottom two rows show binary threshold indicators: S(1)_i / S(1)_max >= 0.1 (relative rule) and S(1)_i > 0.06 (absolute empirical rule). The title reports S(1)_max. Saves the figure in the fmt format.

Parameters:

Name Type Description Default so1_entropies list[tuple[int, float]]

List of (orbital_index, entropy) tuples with the absolute single-orbital entropies; the relative values are computed here by dividing by their maximum.

required n_occ int

Number of occupied orbitals. When non-zero, a dashed vertical line is drawn at n_occ - 0.5 to mark the occupied/virtual boundary.

0 folder str

Directory where the PDF is saved.

'./' filename str

Base name of the output file (without extension).

'SOE_plot' fmt str | None

Output format for the figure (e.g., "pdf", "png"). If None, no extension is appended and matplotlib takes the format from the filename's extension, falling back to rcParams["savefig.format"].

'pdf' Source code in src/aegiss/utils/plotting.py 
def soe_heatmap(
    so1_entropies: list[tuple[int, float]],
    n_occ: int = 0,
    folder: str = "./",
    filename: str = "SOE_plot",
    fmt: str | None = "pdf",
) -> None:
    """Plot a single-orbital entropy (SOE) heatmap.

    Displays a 5-row matrix where the top three rows show the absolute S(1)
    values on a fixed [0, 1] colormap, and the bottom two rows show binary
    threshold indicators: ``S(1)_i / S(1)_max >= 0.1`` (relative rule) and
    ``S(1)_i > 0.06`` (absolute empirical rule). The title reports
    ``S(1)_max``. Saves the figure in the *fmt* format.

    Args:
        so1_entropies: List of (orbital_index, entropy) tuples with the absolute
            single-orbital entropies; the relative values are computed here by
            dividing by their maximum.
        n_occ: Number of occupied orbitals. When non-zero, a dashed vertical line is
            drawn at ``n_occ - 0.5`` to mark the occupied/virtual boundary.
        folder: Directory where the PDF is saved.
        filename: Base name of the output file (without extension).
        fmt: Output format for the figure (e.g., ``"pdf"``, ``"png"``).
            If ``None``, no extension is
            appended and matplotlib takes the format from the filename's
            extension, falling back to ``rcParams["savefig.format"]``.
    """
    so1_abs = np.array([x[1] for x in so1_entropies])
    max_so1 = max(so1_abs)
    so1_rel = so1_abs / max_so1
    large_cas = len(so1_entropies)

    data = np.vstack(
        [
            so1_abs,
            so1_abs,
            so1_abs,
            (so1_rel >= 0.1).astype(float),
            (so1_abs > 0.06).astype(float),
        ]
    )
    fig, ax = plt.subplots(figsize=(8, 3))
    im = ax.imshow(
        data, cmap="magma", aspect="auto", vmin=0, vmax=1, interpolation="nearest"
    )
    fig.colorbar(
        im,
        ax=ax,
        orientation="vertical",
        fraction=0.02,
        pad=0.04,
        label=r"$S(1)_i\,/\,S(1)_\mathrm{max}$",
    )

    ax.set_yticks([1, 3, 4])
    ax.set_yticklabels([r"$S(1)_i$", r"$\tau_{E}$", r"$Emp$"], fontsize=16)
    ax.set_xticks(np.arange(large_cas))
    ax.set_xticklabels(
        [str(to_display(i[0])) for i in so1_entropies], fontsize=10, rotation=90
    )
    ax.set_xlim(-0.5, large_cas - 0.5)
    ax.xaxis.set_ticks_position("bottom")

    if n_occ:
        ax.axvline(x=n_occ - 0.5, ymin=0.4, color="red", linestyle="--", linewidth=4)
    ax.axhline(y=2.5, color="red", linewidth=2)
    ax.axhline(y=3.5, color="red", linewidth=2)

    ax.set_title(f"Max SOE: {max_so1:.5f}", fontsize=16)
    full_filename = f"{filename}.{fmt}" if fmt else filename
    fig.tight_layout()
    fig.savefig(Path(folder) / full_filename, format=fmt, bbox_inches="tight")
    plt.close(fig)
