docs.text:
Plot the threshold curve for single-orbital entropy (TH) analysis.

For each threshold value τ ∈ [0, 1] (as a fraction of S(1)_max), computes the number of orbitals whose relative entropy exceeds τ and plots the resulting staircase curve. Plateau regions — where the orbital count is stable across a range of thresholds — are highlighted and annotated with the implied CAS(n_elec, n_orbs) sizes. Horizontal guides mark the orbital count of the absolute empirical rule (S(1)_i > 0.06) and of the 0.1 * S(1)_max threshold. Saves the figure in the fmt format.

Parameters:

Name Type Description Default so1_entropies list[tuple[int, float]]

List of (orbital_index, entropy) tuples with the absolute single-orbital entropies; they are divided by their maximum here.

required folder str

Directory where the PDF is saved.

'./' occ_index int

Index of the first virtual orbital (HOMO + 1). Orbitals with an index below this are treated as occupied when computing the implied CAS electron count.

0 plateau_size int

Minimum number of consecutive threshold steps (out of 101) for a flat region to be considered a plateau and annotated on the plot.

10 filename str

Base name of the output file (without extension).

'TH_plot' fmt str | None

Output format for the figure (e.g., "pdf", "png"). If None, no extension is appended and matplotlib takes the format from the filename's extension, falling back to rcParams["savefig.format"].

'pdf' Source code in src/aegiss/utils/plotting.py 
def th_plots(
    so1_entropies: list[tuple[int, float]],
    folder: str = "./",
    occ_index: int = 0,
    plateau_size: int = 10,
    filename: str = "TH_plot",
    fmt: str | None = "pdf",
) -> None:
    """Plot the threshold curve for single-orbital entropy (TH) analysis.

    For each threshold value τ ∈ [0, 1] (as a fraction of S(1)_max), computes
    the number of orbitals whose relative entropy exceeds τ and plots the
    resulting staircase curve. Plateau regions — where the orbital count is
    stable across a range of thresholds — are highlighted and annotated with
    the implied CAS(n_elec, n_orbs) sizes. Horizontal guides mark the
    orbital count of the absolute empirical rule (``S(1)_i > 0.06``) and of
    the ``0.1 * S(1)_max`` threshold. Saves the figure in the *fmt* format.

    Args:
        so1_entropies: List of (orbital_index, entropy) tuples with the absolute
            single-orbital entropies; they are divided by their maximum here.
        folder: Directory where the PDF is saved.
        occ_index: Index of the first virtual orbital (HOMO + 1). Orbitals with an index
            below this are treated as occupied when computing the implied CAS electron count.
        plateau_size: Minimum number of consecutive threshold steps (out of 101) for a
            flat region to be considered a plateau and annotated on the plot.
        filename: Base name of the output file (without extension).
        fmt: Output format for the figure (e.g., ``"pdf"``, ``"png"``).
            If ``None``, no extension is
            appended and matplotlib takes the format from the filename's
            extension, falling back to ``rcParams["savefig.format"]``.
    """
    so1_abs = np.array([x[1] for x in so1_entropies])
    max_so1 = max(so1_abs)
    so1_rel = so1_abs / max_so1
    large_cas = len(so1_entropies)
    orbitals_index = np.array([x[0] for x in so1_entropies])

    thumb_rule = int(np.sum(so1_abs > 0.06))
    shade = int(np.sum(so1_rel >= 0.1))

    x_values = np.arange(0, 1.01, 0.01)
    y_values = np.zeros(101)
    indices_above: dict[int, np.ndarray] = {}
    for i, x_value in enumerate(x_values):
        mask = so1_rel > x_value
        indices_above[i] = orbitals_index[mask]
        y_values[i] = int(np.sum(mask))

    plateau_vector, plateau_index, starting_plateaus_indices, rect_size = (
        _detect_plateaus(y_values, indices_above, plateau_size)
    )

    fig, ax = plt.subplots(figsize=(10, 5))
    c = sns.color_palette("magma")

    ax.fill_between(np.arange(-0.05, 1.06, 0.01), shade, 100, color="grey", alpha=0.3)
    ax.plot(x_values, y_values, marker="s", markersize=6, ls="", color=c[0])
    ax.plot(
        plateau_index, plateau_vector, ls="", marker="X", color="white", markersize=5
    )
    ax.set_ylabel("# Selected MOs", fontsize=20)
    ax.set_xlabel(r"Threshold as % of largest $S(1)_\mathrm{max}$", fontsize=18)
    ax.grid(visible=True, alpha=0.3)

    if large_cas > 50:
        ax.set_yticks(np.arange(0, large_cas + 1, 5))
        ax.tick_params(axis="y", labelsize=14)
        ax.set_ylim(0, shade)
    else:
        ax.set_yticks(np.arange(0, large_cas + 1, 2))
        ax.tick_params(axis="y", labelsize=12)
        ax.set_ylim(0, large_cas + 2)

    ax.set_xticks(np.arange(0, 1.1, 0.1))
    ax.tick_params(axis="x", labelsize=18)
    ax.set_xlim(-0.05, 1.05)
    ax.annotate(
        xy=(0.82, thumb_rule + 0.6), text="Empirical", fontsize=16, color="purple"
    )
    ax.annotate(
        xy=(0.82, shade + 0.6),
        text=r"$0.1\cdot S(1)_\mathrm{max}$",
        fontsize=16,
        color="grey",
    )
    ax.axhline(y=thumb_rule, color="purple", linestyle="--", zorder=0)
    ax.axhline(y=y_values[10], color="grey", linestyle="--", zorder=0)

    for i, idx in enumerate(starting_plateaus_indices):
        cas = _define_cas_size(indices_above[idx], occ_index=occ_index)
        x_start, x_end, n_orbs = rect_size[i]
        width = x_end - x_start
        d = 1.5 if large_cas > 40 else 0.5
        rect = patches.Rectangle(
            (x_start, n_orbs - d),
            width,
            2 * d,
            edgecolor="teal",
            facecolor="none",
        )
        ax.add_patch(rect)
        ax.annotate(
            xy=(x_start + width / 2, y_values[idx] + d * 2.5),
            text=f"P#{i + 1}\nCAS({cas[1]},{cas[0]})",
            ha="center",
            fontsize=14,
            color="teal",
            backgroundcolor="white",
            bbox={"edgecolor": "teal", "facecolor": "white"},
        )
        logger.info(
            "\nPlateau #%d:\nN_MOs: %d\nList of MOs: %s\n",
            i + 1,
            len(indices_above[idx]),
            indices_above[idx],
        )

    full_filename = f"{filename}.{fmt}" if fmt else filename
    fig.tight_layout()
    fig.savefig(Path(folder) / full_filename, format=fmt)
    plt.close(fig)

Plot AO contributions as a heatmap, one row per AO group.

Rows share a common [0, 1] colour scale; normalization sets the reference (see below).

When ao_contributions_beta is supplied (unrestricted case), each AO group is shown as a pair of interleaved rows — alpha above beta — and a thin white line separates consecutive groups.

Parameters:

Dict mapping integer group index to a list of (orbital_index, weight) pairs covering all orbitals in the search space. For unrestricted calculations these are the alpha-spin contributions.

required ao_contributions_beta dict[int, list[tuple[int, float]]] | None

Optional beta-spin contributions with the same structure and group keys as ao_contributions. When None (default), a single row per group is drawn (restricted case).

None folder str

Directory where the file is saved.

'./' filename str

Base name of the output file (without extension); _heatmap is appended automatically.

'ao_contribution' ao_labels dict[int, str | list[str]] | None

Dict mapping each group index to its label string (or list of strings, which are joined with newlines). When None (default), letter identifiers A, B, C, … are used as y-tick labels.

None mo_labels list[int] | ndarray | None

Orbital indices to use as x-tick labels. Defaults to sequential integers when None.

None mos_per_plot int

Maximum number of MOs shown in each subplot panel.

Output format for the figure (e.g., "pdf", "png"). If None, no extension is appended and matplotlib takes the format from the filename's extension, falling back to rcParams["savefig.format"].

'pdf' normalization Literal['global', 'relative']

"global" (default) divides every row by the single maximum across the whole matrix, preserving magnitude differences between AO groups. "relative" normalises each group by its own maximum (jointly over alpha and beta), emphasising within-group patterns instead.

    (see below).

    When *ao_contributions_beta* is supplied (unrestricted case), each AO group
    is shown as a pair of interleaved rows — alpha above beta — and a thin white
    line separates consecutive groups.

    Args:
        ao_contributions: Dict mapping integer group index to a list of (orbital_index, weight)

            as *ao_contributions*. When ``None`` (default), a single row per group

        folder: Directory where the file is saved.
        filename: Base name of the output file (without extension); ``_heatmap`` is
            appended automatically.
        ao_labels: Dict mapping each group index to its label string (or list of strings,
            which are joined with newlines). When *None* (default), letter
            identifiers A, B, C, … are used as y-tick labels.
        mo_labels: Orbital indices to use as x-tick labels. Defaults to sequential
            integers when *None*.
        mos_per_plot: Maximum number of MOs shown in each subplot panel.
        fmt: Output format for the figure (e.g., ``"pdf"``, ``"png"``).
            If ``None``, no extension is
            appended and matplotlib takes the format from the filename's
            extension, falling back to ``rcParams["savefig.format"]``.
        normalization: ``"global"`` (default) divides every row by the single maximum across
            the whole matrix, preserving magnitude differences between AO groups.
            ``"relative"`` normalises each group by its own maximum (jointly over
            alpha and beta), emphasising within-group patterns instead.
    """
    matrix, valid_yticks, boundaries = _build_ao_heatmap_matrix(
        ao_contributions, ao_contributions_beta, ao_labels, normalization
    )
    if matrix.size == 0:
        return

    n_mos = matrix.shape[1]
    n_plots = int(np.ceil(n_mos / mos_per_plot))
    vmin, vmax = 0.0, 1.0

    fig = plt.figure(figsize=(25, 3 * n_plots))
    gs = fig.add_gridspec(n_plots, 1, wspace=0.3, hspace=0.25)

    for i in range(n_plots):
        start = i * mos_per_plot
        end = min(start + mos_per_plot, n_mos)
        subset = matrix[:, start:end]

        ax = fig.add_subplot(gs[i, 0])
        sns.heatmap(
            subset,
            ax=ax,
            cbar=False,
            cmap="magma",
            vmin=vmin,
            vmax=vmax,
            yticklabels=valid_yticks,
        )
        ax.set_ylabel("Atomic Orbitals")
        ax.set_xticks(np.arange(end - start) + 0.5)
        if mo_labels is not None:
            ax.set_xticklabels(
                [str(to_display(m)) for m in mo_labels[start:end]], rotation=90
            )
        if ao_contributions_beta is not None:
            for boundary in boundaries[:-1]:
                ax.axhline(boundary, color="white", linewidth=2)

    cbar_ax = fig.add_axes((0.92, 0.15, 0.02, 0.7))
    sm = plt.cm.ScalarMappable(
        cmap="magma", norm=mcolors.Normalize(vmin=vmin, vmax=vmax)
    )
    sm.set_array([])
    fig.colorbar(sm, cax=cbar_ax)

    stem = f"{filename}_heatmap"
    full_filename = f"{stem}.{fmt}" if fmt else stem
    plt.subplots_adjust(left=0.1, right=0.9, top=0.9, bottom=0.1)
    fig.savefig(Path(folder) / full_filename, format=fmt, bbox_inches="tight")
    plt.close(fig)

def plot_pie_contribution(
    mol: pyscf.gto.Mole,
    mf: Any,
    ao_labels: list[str | list[str]] | str,
    labels_names: list[str | list[str]],
    orbs: list[int] | np.ndarray,
    filename: str = "composition",
    folder: str = "./",
    orb_for_row: int = 4,
    min_pct: float = 0.01,
    fmt: str | None = "pdf",
) -> None:
    """Plot per-orbital AO composition as a grid of pie charts.

    For each orbital in *orbs*, draws a pie chart showing the fractional
    contribution of each AO group defined in *ao_labels*. Slices whose
    contribution is below *min_pct* are rendered without label or percentage.
    Saves one PDF per spin channel (``_alpha`` / ``_beta`` for unrestricted,
    ``_alpha`` only for restricted).

    Args:
        mol: PySCF Mole object, used to resolve AO labels.
        mf: Converged mean-field object. ``mf.mo_coeff`` may be ``(n_ao, n_mo)``
            (restricted) or ``(2, n_ao, n_mo)`` (unrestricted).
        ao_labels: AO label strings recognised by ``mol.search_ao_label``,
            e.g. ``["C 2pz", "Fe 3d"]``. A bare string is wrapped into a list.
        labels_names: Human-readable names for each entry in *ao_labels*, used as pie
            slice labels. Must have the same length as *ao_labels*.
        orbs: Indices of the molecular orbitals to plot.
        filename: Base name for the output PDF (spin suffix appended automatically).
        folder: Directory where the PDF is saved.
        orb_for_row: Number of orbitals per row in the subplot grid.
        min_pct: Minimum fractional contribution (0-1) below which the slice label
            and percentage are hidden. Default is 0.01 (1 %).
        fmt: Output format for the figure (e.g., "pdf", "png").
            If ``None``, no extension is
            appended and matplotlib takes the format from the filename's
            extension, falling back to ``rcParams["savefig.format"]``.
    """
    if isinstance(ao_labels, str):
        ao_labels = [ao_labels]
    if len(ao_labels) != len(labels_names):
        raise ValueError(
            f"ao_labels and labels_names must have the same length, "
            f"got {len(ao_labels)} and {len(labels_names)}."
        )
    if len(orbs) == 0:
        raise ValueError("orbs must not be empty.")
    if orb_for_row <= 0:
        raise ValueError(f"orb_for_row must be a positive integer, got {orb_for_row}.")

    str_labels_names = [" ".join(n) if isinstance(n, list) else n for n in labels_names]
    shape = (int(np.ceil(len(orbs) / orb_for_row)), orb_for_row)
    common = {
        "shape": shape,
        "mol": mol,
        "orbs": orbs,
        "ao_labels": ao_labels,
        "labels_names": str_labels_names,
        "folder": folder,
        "min_pct": min_pct,
        "fmt": fmt,
    }

    if np.ndim(mf.mo_coeff) == 3:
        moa, mob = mf.mo_coeff
        _save_contributions(**common, mo=moa, filename=filename + "_alpha")
        _save_contributions(**common, mo=mob, filename=filename + "_beta")
    else:
        _save_contributions(**common, mo=mf.mo_coeff, filename=filename + "_alpha")

def mi_plot(
    minfo: np.ndarray,
    soe1: list[tuple[int, float]],
    folder: str = "./",
    filename: str = "MI_plot",
    fmt: str | None = "pdf",
) -> None:
    """Plot the orbital mutual-information (MI) matrix as a heatmap.

    The AEGISS pipeline computes single-orbital entropies only, so *minfo* must
    come from an external calculation, for example
    ``DMRGDriver.get_orbital_interaction_matrix`` in block2's Python API. The
    colour scale runs from 0 to the largest element of *minfo*, so the diagonal
    should be zero.

    Args:
        minfo: Symmetric ``(n, n)`` MI matrix. Row and column ``k`` belong to the
            orbital ``soe1[k][0]``.
        soe1: List of (orbital_index, single_orbital_entropy) tuples for all
            orbitals, in the row order of *minfo*. Only the indices are used,
            as tick labels (shown in the configured orbital index base).
        folder: Directory where the PDF is saved.
        filename: Base name of the output file (without extension).
        fmt: Output format for the figure (e.g., ``"pdf"``, ``"png"``).
            If ``None``, no extension is
            appended and matplotlib takes the format from the filename's
            extension, falling back to ``rcParams["savefig.format"]``.
    """
    fig, ax = plt.subplots(figsize=(8, 8))
    ax.matshow(minfo, cmap="magma", vmin=0, vmax=np.max(minfo))
    plt.colorbar(
        ax.imshow(minfo, cmap="magma", vmin=0, vmax=np.max(minfo)),
        ax=ax,
        fraction=0.02,
        pad=0.04,
        label="Mutual Information (MI)",
    )

    _ticks_helper(soe1, ax)
    ax.set_xlabel("Orbital Index", fontsize=12)
    ax.set_ylabel("Orbital Index", fontsize=12)

    full_filename = f"{filename}.{fmt}" if fmt else filename
    fig.tight_layout()
    fig.savefig(Path(folder) / full_filename, format=fmt, bbox_inches="tight")
    logger.info("Saved %s", full_filename)
    plt.close(fig)

Plot entanglement diagrams for active and virtual orbitals.

Each orbital is drawn as a marker on a circle, all in the same colour. The marker size grows in fixed steps with the orbital's single-orbital entropy (SOE) relative to the largest SOE, in 5% bins; orbitals below 5% of the maximum get no marker. Solid to dotted is the gradient for the Mutual Information (MI) between orbitals. The plot is saved in the fmt format.

The AEGISS pipeline computes single-orbital entropies only, so minfo must come from an external calculation, for example DMRGDriver.get_orbital_interaction_matrix in block2's Python API. MI values are normalised by their maximum before the line styles are chosen (thresholds 1, 0.1, 0.01 and 0.001 of the maximum), so the overall scale and the MI convention (with or without the factor 1/2) do not matter.

required folder str, default "./"

def entanglement_diagrams(
    soe1: list[tuple[Any, Any]],
    minfo: np.ndarray,
    folder: str = "./",
    filename: str = "entanglement_diagrams",
    fmt: str | None = "pdf",
) -> None:
    """Plot entanglement diagrams for active and virtual orbitals.

    Each orbital is drawn as a marker on a circle, all in the same colour. The
    marker size grows in fixed steps with the orbital's single-orbital entropy
    (SOE) relative to the largest SOE, in 5% bins; orbitals below 5% of the
    maximum get no marker. Solid to dotted is the gradient for the Mutual
    Information (MI) between orbitals. The plot is saved in the *fmt* format.

    The AEGISS pipeline computes single-orbital entropies only, so *minfo* must
    come from an external calculation, for example
    ``DMRGDriver.get_orbital_interaction_matrix`` in block2's Python API. MI
    values are normalised by their maximum before the line styles are chosen
    (thresholds 1, 0.1, 0.01 and 0.001 of the maximum), so the overall scale
    and the MI convention (with or without the factor 1/2) do not matter.

    Args:
        soe1 (list of tuples): List of (orbital_index, single_orbital_entropy) tuples for all orbitals,
            in the row order of *minfo*.
        minfo (np.ndarray): Symmetric ``(n, n)`` Mutual Information matrix between the orbitals of
            *soe1*. Only the upper triangle is read, so the diagonal is ignored.
        folder (str, default "./"): Directory where the PDF file will be saved.
        filename (str, default "entanglement_diagrams"): Base name of the output PDF file (without extension).
        fmt (str or None, default "pdf"): Output format for the figure (e.g., ``"pdf"``, ``"png"``).
            If ``None``, no extension is appended and matplotlib takes the
            format from the filename's extension, falling back to
            ``rcParams["savefig.format"]``.
    """
    N = len(soe1)

    angles = np.linspace(0, 2 * np.pi, N, endpoint=False)
    x = np.cos(angles)
    y = np.sin(angles)

    fig, ax = plt.subplots(figsize=(6, 6))
    ax.set_aspect("equal")
    ax.axis("off")

    circle1 = plt.Circle((0, 0), 1.25, color="black", fill=False, linewidth=1)
    circle2 = plt.Circle((0, 0), 1, color="black", fill=False, linewidth=2)
    ax.add_patch(circle1)
    ax.add_patch(circle2)

    # mi thresholds

    handles_mi = _helper_mi(minfo, x, y, ax)
    handler_soe = _helper_soe(soe1, x, y, ax)
    handles = handles_mi + handler_soe

    leg = plt.legend(handles=handles, loc="center")
    leg.get_frame().set_alpha(None)
    full_filename = f"{filename}.{fmt}" if fmt else filename
    fig.tight_layout()
    fig.savefig(Path(folder) / full_filename, format=fmt, bbox_inches="tight")
    logger.info("Saved %s", full_filename)
    plt.close(fig)

def mem() -> int:
    """Return ``stack_mem`` in bytes from the ``MEM`` environment variable.

    ``MEM`` must be a positive integer number of GiB. If it is unset, not a
    valid integer, zero, or negative, the default of ``_DEFAULT_MEM_GIB`` GiB
    is used instead. Invalid and non-positive values cause a warning to be
    logged before falling back to the default.

    Returns:
        int: The amount of memory in bytes to use for DMRG stack memory.
    """
    raw = os.environ.get("MEM")
    if raw is None:
        return _DEFAULT_MEM_GIB * (1 << 30)

    stripped = raw.strip()
    try:
        mem_gib = int(stripped)
    except ValueError:
        logger.warning(
            "MEM=%r is not a valid integer; using default %d GiB.",
            stripped,
            _DEFAULT_MEM_GIB,
        )
        return _DEFAULT_MEM_GIB * (1 << 30)

    if mem_gib <= 0:
        logger.warning(
            "MEM=%d is not a positive integer; using default %d GiB.",
            mem_gib,
            _DEFAULT_MEM_GIB,
        )
        return _DEFAULT_MEM_GIB * (1 << 30)

    return mem_gib * (1 << 30)

def configure_logging(
    level: int = logging.INFO,
    timestamp_fmt: str = TIMESTAMP_FMT,
) -> None:
    """Configure structlog over stdlib logging, writing to stdout.

    Replaces any handlers on the root logger and clamps noisy third-party
    loggers (matplotlib, h5py) to ``WARNING``. Redirect stdout from the shell to
    control the destination:

        python main.py > log.out        # local
        #SBATCH -o slurm-%j.out         # SLURM

    Args:
        level (int): Root logger level (default ``logging.INFO``).
        timestamp_fmt (str): ``strftime`` format for the timestamp of each log
            line (default ``"%Y-%m-%d %H:%M:%S"``).
    """
    shared_processors: list[Processor] = [
        structlog.stdlib.add_log_level,
        structlog.processors.TimeStamper(fmt=timestamp_fmt),
        structlog.stdlib.PositionalArgumentsFormatter(),
    ]

    structlog.configure(
        processors=[
            *shared_processors,
            structlog.stdlib.ProcessorFormatter.wrap_for_formatter,
        ],
        logger_factory=structlog.stdlib.LoggerFactory(),
        wrapper_class=structlog.stdlib.BoundLogger,
        cache_logger_on_first_use=True,
    )

    formatter = structlog.stdlib.ProcessorFormatter(
        processor=structlog.dev.ConsoleRenderer(colors=False),
        foreign_pre_chain=shared_processors,
    )

    handler = logging.StreamHandler(sys.stdout)
    handler.setFormatter(formatter)

    root = logging.getLogger()
    root.handlers.clear()
    root.setLevel(level)
    root.addHandler(handler)

    for name in _SILENCED:
        logging.getLogger(name).setLevel(logging.WARNING)

docs.text:
Run a DMRG calculation via the block2main subprocess.

Parameters:

Name Type Description Default mf SCF

Converged mean-field object.

required ncas int

Number of active orbitals.

required nelecas int or tuple[int, int]

Number of active electrons (total count or (nalpha, nbeta) pair).

required max_bond_dim int

Target bond dimension for the DMRG schedule (must be a positive multiple of 4).

500 symm_type {'SU2', 'SZ'}

Spin symmetry: 'SZ' adds the nonspinadapted keyword so block2main runs without spin adaptation; 'SU2' omits it.

'SZ' verbosity int

If non-zero, block2main stdout/stderr are forwarded to the terminal.

0 unrestricted bool or None

Whether to emit an unrestricted (UHF, IUHF=1) FCIDUMP with separate aa/bb/ab and alpha/beta blocks. If None (default), autodetected from isinstance(mf, scf.uhf.UHF); pass True/False to override. UHF requires symm_type='SZ'.

None get_qmi bool

If True, compute and return single-orbital entropies.

True spin_resolved bool

If True, return separate alpha/beta spin-orbital entropies as a (2, ncas) array (row 0 = alpha, row 1 = beta) instead of the spin-summed (ncas,) vector. Only meaningful with get_qmi. The spin-summed vector feeds :func:~aegiss.active_space.entropy_screening.select_by_entropy; the (2, ncas) array feeds :func:~aegiss.active_space.entropy_screening.select_by_spin_entropy. :func:~aegiss.active_space.aegiss.select_aegiss sets this from :meth:DMRGConfig.spin_resolved.

False reorder {'noreorder', 'fiedler'}

Orbital ordering for block2main. 'noreorder' (default) keeps the FCIDUMP order and enables full_fci_space; 'fiedler' reorders by the Fiedler vector and disables full_fci_space (that combination can converge to a higher local minimum). Output 1pdm/1npc are mapped back to the input order either way, so per-orbital entropy indexing is unaffected.

'noreorder'

Returns:

Name Type Description energy float

DMRG ground-state energy.

soe1 ndarray or None

Single-orbital entropies (None if get_qmi is False). Shape (ncas,) by default, or (2, ncas) if spin_resolved is True. Two-orbital entropies and mutual information are not available from the 1pdm + 1npc output; pass them from an external source to any downstream plotting functions if needed.

Raises:

Type Description ValueError

def run_dmrg_subprocess(
    mf: Any,
    ncas: int,
    nelecas: int | tuple[int, int],
    max_bond_dim: int = 500,
    symm_type: str = "SZ",
    verbosity: int = 0,
    *,
    unrestricted: bool | None = None,
    get_qmi: bool = True,
    spin_resolved: bool = False,
    reorder: str = "noreorder",
) -> tuple[float, np.ndarray | None]:
    """Run a DMRG calculation via the ``block2main`` subprocess.

    Args:
        mf (pyscf.scf.hf.SCF): Converged mean-field object.
        ncas (int): Number of active orbitals.
        nelecas (int or tuple[int, int]): Number of active electrons (total
            count or ``(nalpha, nbeta)`` pair).
        max_bond_dim (int): Target bond dimension for the DMRG schedule (must
            be a positive multiple of 4).
        symm_type ({'SU2', 'SZ'}): Spin symmetry: ``'SZ'`` adds the
            ``nonspinadapted`` keyword so block2main runs without spin
            adaptation; ``'SU2'`` omits it.
        verbosity (int): If non-zero, block2main stdout/stderr are forwarded to
            the terminal.
        unrestricted (bool or None): Whether to emit an unrestricted (UHF,
            ``IUHF=1``) FCIDUMP with separate aa/bb/ab and alpha/beta blocks. If
            ``None`` (default), autodetected from ``isinstance(mf, scf.uhf.UHF)``;
            pass ``True``/``False`` to override. UHF requires ``symm_type='SZ'``.
        get_qmi (bool): If ``True``, compute and return single-orbital
            entropies.
        spin_resolved (bool): If ``True``, return separate alpha/beta
            spin-orbital entropies as a ``(2, ncas)`` array (row 0 = alpha,
            row 1 = beta) instead of the spin-summed ``(ncas,)`` vector. Only
            meaningful with *get_qmi*. The spin-summed vector feeds
            :func:`~aegiss.active_space.entropy_screening.select_by_entropy`;
            the ``(2, ncas)`` array feeds
            :func:`~aegiss.active_space.entropy_screening.select_by_spin_entropy`.
            :func:`~aegiss.active_space.aegiss.select_aegiss` sets this from
            :meth:`DMRGConfig.spin_resolved`.
        reorder ({'noreorder', 'fiedler'}): Orbital ordering for block2main.
            ``'noreorder'`` (default) keeps the FCIDUMP order and enables
            ``full_fci_space``; ``'fiedler'`` reorders by the Fiedler vector and
            disables ``full_fci_space`` (that combination can converge to a
            higher local minimum). Output ``1pdm``/``1npc`` are mapped back to
            the input order either way, so per-orbital entropy indexing is
            unaffected.

    Returns:
        energy (float): DMRG ground-state energy.
        soe1 (np.ndarray or None): Single-orbital entropies (``None`` if
            *get_qmi* is ``False``). Shape ``(ncas,)`` by default, or
            ``(2, ncas)`` if *spin_resolved* is ``True``. Two-orbital entropies
            and mutual information are not available from the ``1pdm`` +
            ``1npc`` output; pass them from an external source to any downstream
            plotting functions if needed.

    Raises:
        ValueError: If *symm_type* or *reorder* is not a supported value, if
            *unrestricted* is used with ``symm_type='SU2'``, or if
            *max_bond_dim* is not a positive multiple of 4.
        RuntimeError: If the ``block2main`` executable cannot be found.
        subprocess.CalledProcessError: If ``block2main`` exits with a non-zero
            status.
    """
    if symm_type not in _VALID_SYMM_TYPES:
        raise ValueError(
            f"Unsupported symmetry type: {symm_type!r}. Expected one of {list(_VALID_SYMM_TYPES)}."
        )
    if reorder not in _VALID_REORDER:
        raise ValueError(
            f"Unsupported reorder: {reorder!r}. Expected one of {list(_VALID_REORDER)}."
        )

    if unrestricted is None:
        unrestricted = isinstance(mf, scf.uhf.UHF)
    if unrestricted and symm_type != "SZ":
        raise ValueError(
            f"Unrestricted (UHF) integrals require symm_type='SZ', got {symm_type!r}. "
            "block2 cannot read an IUHF=1 FCIDUMP in a spin-adapted (SU2) run."
        )

    scratch = get_scratch_dir()
    n_threads = omp_num_threads()
    stack_mem_gb = mem() / (1024**3)

    bond_dims, noises, thrds = _default_dmrg_schedule(max_bond_dim)
    nalpha, nbeta = resolve_nelecas(nelecas)
    n_sweeps = len(bond_dims)
    twosite_to_onesite = max(n_sweeps - 2, 0)

    logger.info(
        "----------------DMRG Calculation (symmetry: %s)----------------\n", symm_type
    )
    logger.info(
        "Using pyscf.%s to obtain integrals for DMRG...",
        "UCASCI" if unrestricted else "CASCI",
    )
    logger.info("CAS (ncas=%d, nelecas=%s)", ncas, nelecas)
    logger.info(
        "System parameters: n_sites=%d, n_elec=%d, spin=%d, symm_type=%s",
        ncas,
        nalpha + nbeta,
        nalpha - nbeta,
        symm_type,
    )
    logger.info("Scratch directory: %s", scratch)
    logger.info("Number of threads: %d", n_threads)
    logger.info(
        "DMRG settings: n_sweeps = %d, max_bond_dim = %d, twosite_to_onesite = %d",
        n_sweeps,
        max_bond_dim,
        twosite_to_onesite,
    )
    logger.info("DMRG Noise: init = %s, final = %s", noises[0], noises[-1])
    logger.info("DMRG Threshold: init = %s, final = %s\n", thrds[0], thrds[-1])

    work_dir = Path(scratch) / f"dmrg_subprocess_{time.time_ns()}"
    work_dir.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=False)
    fcidump_path = work_dir / "FCIDUMP"
    if unrestricted:
        _write_uhf_fcidump(fcidump_path, mf, ncas, (nalpha, nbeta))
    else:
        _write_fcidump(fcidump_path, mf, ncas, nelecas)

    input_path = work_dir / "dmrg.conf"
    _write_input(
        input_path,
        fcidump_path,
        nalpha + nbeta,
        nalpha - nbeta,
        ncas,
        work_dir,
        bond_dims,
        noises,
        thrds,
        n_threads,
        stack_mem_gb,
        symm_type,
        reorder,
    )

    _venv_bin = Path(sys.executable).parent
    block2main_path = shutil.which("block2main") or (
        str(_venv_bin / "block2main") if (_venv_bin / "block2main").exists() else None
    )
    if block2main_path is None:
        raise RuntimeError(
            "block2main not found in PATH or venv bin directory. "
            "Activate the project venv or add block2main to PATH."
        )

    logger.info("Running block2main: %s %s", block2main_path, input_path)
    t = time.time()
    subprocess.run(  # noqa: S603
        [block2main_path, str(input_path)],
        capture_output=(verbosity == 0),
        check=True,
    )
    logger.info("DMRG completed in %.3f [s]", time.time() - t)

    energy, pdm1, npc1 = _read_outputs(work_dir, ncas)
    logger.info("DMRG Energy (%s)\t : %.8f", symm_type, energy)

    if not get_qmi:
        return energy, None

    soe1 = _compute_spin_soe(pdm1) if spin_resolved else _compute_soe(pdm1, npc1)
    return energy, soe1

docs.title: Tutorials
docs.text:
The tutorials walk through the full AEGISS workflow using benzene as a running example. Each notebook is self-contained and builds on the previous one. The input geometries used by the notebooks live alongside them in docs/tutorials/data/.

Notebook Topic 01 — SCF & Localization Building the molecule, running HF/DFT, scalar relativistic corrections (X2C), orbital localization (Boys, PM, ER, IBOs, IAOs, NOs, FNOs) 02 — DMRG & Entropy DMRGConfig, running DMRG, inspecting single-orbital entropies, entropy screening 03 — AO Projection ProjectionConfig, AO-projection selection, thresholds and top-N ranking 04 — Full Pipeline End-to-end AEGISS pipeline with all four config objects 05 — Unrestricted (UHF) What changes for a UHF reference: 3-D mo_coeff, symm_type="SZ", spin_soe, split α/β selection, per-channel thresholds

docs.title: Inputs
docs.text:
• Molecular structure: \(\{\mathcal{R}\}\)
  • Mean-field method and basis set
  • Correlated wavefunction method: \(\mathcal{W}\) (DMRG via block2)
  • AO groups: \(\mathcal{D}\) — PySCF ao_labels strings, e.g. "Fe 3d", "C 2pz"
  • Entropy threshold: \(\tau_E\) (default: \(0.1 \times S(1)_{\max}\), configurable)
  • AO cutoff: \(\epsilon_D\) or rank threshold \(n_D\)

docs.title: Output
docs.text: Final active orbital space: \(\{\psi_r\}\)

docs.title: Step 1 — Atom labeling and AO group definition
docs.text:
Partition the molecule into chemically meaningful clusters \(\mathcal{C}_i\) (e.g. metal centre, ligand π system, σ framework). For each cluster define an AO group \(D_i \in \mathcal{D}\) as a set of PySCF ao_labels strings.

MolTagger

aegiss.utils.mol_tagger.MolTagger provides an interactive 3D viewer for selecting atoms and auto-generating ao_labels strings ready to paste into ProjectionConfig.

docs.title: Step 2 — Mean-field calculation
docs.text:
Perform HF or KS-DFT to obtain the MO coefficient matrix \([\mathbf{C}]_{\mu p}\), then select orbitals belonging to the active region \(\mathbf{A}\) defined by the CAS window (ncas, nelecas).

Optional solvation — for molecules in solution, pass solvent_info=(model, dielectric_constant) to run_scf. Two implicit-solvent families are supported (PySCF solvation docs):

Model Key Notes IEF-PCM "IEF-PCM" ISO standard; general purpose C-PCM "C-PCM" Conductor-like limit; slightly cheaper DD-COSMO "DDCOSMO" Linear-scaling; good for large systems 
mf_pcm = run_scf(mol, method="RHF", solvent_info=("IEF-PCM", 78.4))  # water

The solvation wrapper is fully composable with the relativistic parameter and propagates into the DMRG integral step transparently via CASCI.get_h1eff.

Optional scalar relativistic correction — for systems containing transition metals or heavier elements, pass relativistic='x2c' to run_scf to apply the exact two-component (X2C) transformation. The relativistic one-electron Hamiltonian propagates automatically into the DMRG integral step via CASCI.get_h1eff.

mf = run_scf(mol, method="RHF", relativistic="x2c")

Optional orbital localization — canonical MOs can be transformed before DMRG to improve physical interpretability of entropy screening:

Key Method Criterion "boys" Foster–Boys Minimum orbital spread "pm" Pipek–Mezey Maximum atomic charge; preserves σ/π separation "er" Edmiston–Ruedenberg Maximum self-repulsion energy "ibos" Intrinsic Bond Orbitals Maximum population on intrinsic atomic orbitals "iaos" Intrinsic Atomic Orbitals Minimal-basis-like basis of the occupied space (returns the IAO basis, not a replacement for mo_coeff) "nos" Natural Orbitals Diagonalise correlated 1-RDM "fnos" Frozen Natural Orbitals As NOs but with a frozen core

Localized orbitals have no orbital energies, so the index-based CAS window built on them is no longer a Fermi-level window; see the methodology.

docs.title: Step 3a — Correlated wavefunction in active region
docs.text: AEGISS solves the active-space problem with DMRG, run through the block2main subprocess (run_dmrg_subprocess). PySCF builds the CAS integrals (a FCIDUMP) for the active region \(\mathbf{A}\); block2 then converges the DMRG ground state \(|\Psi\rangle\) and writes out the spin-resolved one-particle density matrix (1pdm) and the diagonal number–number correlation (1npc) — together these provide everything needed for the single-orbital entropies below.

docs.title: One-orbital reduced density matrix
docs.text:
For each orbital \(p \in \mathbf{A}\), the one-orbital reduced density matrix \(\rho^p\) is defined by tracing \(|\Psi\rangle\langle\Psi|\) over all orbitals except \(p\):

\[ \rho^p = \mathrm{Tr}_{\mathbf{A} \setminus \{p\}} \left( |\Psi\rangle\langle\Psi| \right) \]

In the local occupation basis \(|\alpha\rangle \in \{|0\rangle,\, |\!\uparrow\rangle,\, |\!\downarrow\rangle,\, |\!\uparrow\downarrow\rangle\}\) a single orbital carries no coherences, so \(\rho^p\) is diagonal and its four eigenvalues are precisely the occupation probabilities \(\{\omega_{\alpha,p}\}\) (with \(\omega_{\alpha,p} \geq 0\) and \(\sum_\alpha \omega_{\alpha,p} = 1\)).

Rather than forming \(\rho^p\) explicitly, AEGISS reconstructs these probabilities from the DMRG one-particle observables: the spin occupations \(\langle n_{p\uparrow}\rangle\), \(\langle n_{p\downarrow}\rangle\) (diagonal of the 1pdm) and the double occupancy \(d_p = \langle n_{p\uparrow} n_{p\downarrow}\rangle\). The double occupancy is recovered from the diagonal of the number–number correlation, since \(\langle n_p^2\rangle = \langle n_p\rangle + 2\,d_p\) for \(n_p = n_{p\uparrow} + n_{p\downarrow}\):

\[ d_p = \tfrac{1}{2}\left(\langle n_p^2\rangle - \langle n_p\rangle\right), \qquad \langle n_p\rangle = \langle n_{p\uparrow}\rangle + \langle n_{p\downarrow}\rangle \]

which fixes the four occupation probabilities as

\[ \begin{aligned} \omega_{\uparrow\downarrow,\,p} &= d_p, & \omega_{\uparrow,\,p} &= \langle n_{p\uparrow}\rangle - d_p, \\[2pt] \omega_{\downarrow,\,p} &= \langle n_{p\downarrow}\rangle - d_p, & \omega_{0,\,p} &= 1 - \langle n_p\rangle + d_p . \end{aligned} \]

docs.title: Step 3b — Entropy-based reduction
docs.text:
For each orbital \(p\), the single-orbital entropy is the von Neumann entropy of \(\rho^p\) — equivalently, the Shannon entropy of its four occupation probabilities:

\[ S(1)_p = -\sum_{\alpha \in \{0,\,\uparrow,\,\downarrow,\,\uparrow\downarrow\}} \omega_{\alpha,p} \, \ln \omega_{\alpha,p} \]

where any state with \(\omega_{\alpha,p} \to 0\) contributes nothing to the sum.

\(S(1)_p\) quantifies the entanglement of orbital \(p\) with the rest of the active space. It is zero for orbitals that are fully occupied or fully empty (doubly occupied core or unoccupied virtual), and maximal for orbitals in a strongly correlated superposition.

Select entropy-active orbitals:

\[ \{\psi^{\mathbf{A}}_{E}\} = \{\psi_p^{\mathbf{A}} \mid S(1)_p \geq \tau_E\} \] fraction_type Threshold \(\tau_E\) 'r' (relative, default) \(\text{fraction} \times S(1)_{\max}\) 'a' (absolute) \(\text{fraction}\) directly

The threshold is applied independently to occupied and virtual subspaces (ranking='subset', default) or to all CAS orbitals jointly (ranking='global').

Diagnostics

The entropy spectrum is best read visually with soe_heatmap and th_plots (utilities reference). For a benzene CAS(30,30), the entanglement concentrates on the π-type frontier orbitals, and the threshold curve exposes two plateaus — CAS(6,6) and, at higher thresholds, the π-only CAS(4,4):

docs.title: Step 4 — AO projection for each group \(D \in \mathcal{D}\)
docs.text: For each AO group \(D\) (e.g. "Fe 3d", "C 2pz"), a weight \(w_p^D\) is assigned to every entropy-filtered orbital \(\psi_p \in \{\psi^{\mathbf{A}}_E\}\) that measures how much of that orbital lives in the target chemical subspace.

docs.title: Cross-overlap matrix \(\mathbf{O}^D_E\)
docs.text:
The projection is performed against a secondary minimal basis (default: minao) rather than the original working basis. Let \(\{\phi^D_\mu\}\) be the AOs of the minimal basis restricted to the atoms and angular-momentum channels defined by \(D\), and let \(\{\phi^E_ u\}\) be the AOs of the original molecular basis. The cross-overlap matrix is:

\[ [\mathbf{O}^D_E]_{\mu u} = \langle \phi^D_\mu \mid \phi^E_ u angle, \qquad \mu \in D,\ u \in E \]

computed via pyscf.gto.intor_cross("int1e_ovlp", ...). Using a minimal basis for \(D\) removes noise from diffuse or polarisation functions that are present in the working basis but are not chemically meaningful for the selection criterion.

docs.title: Projection and weight
docs.text:
The MO coefficients \([\mathbf{C}_E]_{ u p}\) expand each orbital \(\psi_p\) in the original basis. The projection of \(\psi_p\) onto the target AO subspace \(D\) is:

\[ [\mathbf{O}^D_E\,\mathbf{C}_E]_{\mu p} = \sum_{ u \in E} [\mathbf{O}^D_E]_{\mu u}\,[\mathbf{C}_E]_{ u p} = \langle \phi^D_\mu \mid \psi_p angle \]

The weight is the \(\ell^1\) norm of this projection over all \(\mu \in D\):

\[ w_p^D = \sum_{\mu \in D} \left|\langle \phi^D_\mu \mid \psi_p angle ight| = \sum_{\mu \in D} \left|[\mathbf{O}^D_E\,\mathbf{C}_E]_{\mu p} ight| \]

A large \(w_p^D\) means orbital \(\psi_p\) has strong overlap with the target AO characters; a value near zero means it is essentially orthogonal to that subspace.

docs.title: Normalisation
docs.text: contribution_type Weight used for thresholding 'a' (absolute) \(w_p^D\) directly 'r' (relative) \(\tilde{w}_p^D = w_p^D \,/\, \max_{p'} w_{p'}^D \in [0,1]\)

docs.title: Selection
docs.text:
Two modes are available, controlled by ProjectionConfig:

  • Threshold — keep all \(\psi_p\) where \(w_p^D \geq \epsilon_D\)
  • Top-N — keep the \(n_D\) orbitals with the largest \(w_p^D\), regardless of magnitude

Diagnostics

The projection weights \(w_p^D\) can be inspected with plot_ao_contribution (a per-MO / per-AO-group heatmap) and the per-orbital composition with plot_pie_contribution (utilities reference). For benzene, the π orbitals concentrate on C 2pz while the σ framework mixes C 2s/C 2px/H 1s:

docs.title: Step 5 — Active space construction
docs.text:
Merge selected sets across all AO groups:

\[ \{\psi_r\} = \bigcup_{D \in \mathcal{D}} \{\psi_r^D\} \]

docs.title: Tutorial 1 — SCF and Orbital Localization¶
docs.text:
This notebook covers the two preparatory steps that precede any AEGISS active space selection: obtaining a mean-field reference wavefunction and (optionally) transforming the canonical molecular orbitals (MOs) into a localized representation.

Why localize? Canonical HF/KS orbitals are delocalized over the whole molecule by symmetry. Localized orbitals concentrate electron density on chemically relevant fragments, making the subsequent DMRG entropy and AO-projection screening more physically meaningful.

Contents

  1. Imports
  2. Build the molecule
  3. Run RHF (3b. scalar relativistic correction, X2C)
  4. Boys localization
  5. Pipek–Mezey (PM) localization
  6. Edmiston–Ruedenberg (ER) localization
  7. Intrinsic Bond Orbitals (IBOs)
  8. Intrinsic Atomic Orbitals (IAOs)
  9. Natural Orbitals (NOs) from MP2
  10. Frozen Natural Orbitals (FNOs)

docs.title: 2. Build the molecule¶
docs.text: build_mol is a thin wrapper around pyscf.gto.Mole. Any keyword accepted by Mole (e.g. basis, charge, spin, symmetry) can be passed as keyword arguments.

docs.title: 3. Run RHF¶
docs.text: run_scf dispatches to PySCF's RHF, UHF, RKS, or UKS depending on the method argument. It calls kernel() and returns the converged mean-field object.

docs.title: 3b. Scalar relativistic correction (X2C)¶
docs.text:
For molecules containing heavier elements — transition metals, lanthanides, actinides — scalar relativistic effects contract the core s and p shells and alter valence orbital energies noticeably. AEGISS exposes PySCF's exact two-component (X2C) transformation via the relativistic parameter of run_scf.

X2C folds the mass-velocity and Darwin corrections into a modified one-electron Hamiltonian. The rest of the workflow (DMRG integral fetch via CASCI.get_h1eff, entropy screening, AO projection) requires no changes — the relativistic integrals propagate automatically through the mf object.

Basis sets: for production calculations on heavy elements use a relativistically contracted basis (e.g. ano-rcc, dyall-vdz, x2c-svpall) together with relativistic='x2c'. The STO-3G basis used in this tutorial is not optimised for relativistic corrections; the example below illustrates the API only.

docs.title: 4. Boys localization¶
docs.text:
Boys localization minimises the spatial spread \(\langle r^2 \rangle - \langle r \rangle^2\) of each orbital, producing chemically intuitive bond and lone-pair orbitals.

By default only the occupied space is localized. Pass on_virtual=True to also localize the virtual space — useful before entropy screening.

docs.title: 5. Pipek–Mezey (PM) localization¶
docs.text: PM localization maximises the sum of squared Mulliken partial charges on atoms, tending to preserve σ/π separation and produce orbitals tied to specific atoms. It is generally preferred over Boys for systems with distinct bond types.

docs.title: 6. Edmiston–Ruedenberg (ER) localization¶
docs.text: ER localization maximises the orbital self-repulsion energy \(\langle ii | ii \rangle\). It is the most rigorous localization scheme but also the most expensive due to two-electron integral transformations. For large systems prefer Boys or PM.

docs.title: 7. Intrinsic Bond Orbitals (IBOs)¶
docs.text:
IBOs (Knizia, JCTC 2013) localise occupied MOs by maximising their population on Intrinsic Atomic Orbitals (IAOs). They tend to give chemically intuitive bond / lone-pair orbitals, preserve σ/π separation similarly to PM, and are especially well-suited for systems with mixed ionic/covalent character and for transition metals.

IBOs operate only on the occupied space; the virtual block is kept unchanged.

docs.title: 8. Intrinsic Atomic Orbitals (IAOs)¶
docs.text:
IAOs are a set of orthonormal orbitals expressed in the AO basis that closely resemble the functions of a reference minimal basis (default: "minao"). They span the occupied MO space and provide a chemically meaningful atom-centred representation.

IAOs are typically used as:

  • a localized occupied basis for population / charge analysis
  • the underlying population measure inside the IBO construction

There is one IAO per function of the minimal basis, which is in general more than the number of occupied MOs, so localize("iaos") returns the IAO basis itself, of shape (nao, n_iao), not a replacement for mf.mo_coeff.

docs.title: 9. Natural Orbitals (NOs)¶
docs.text:
Natural orbitals diagonalise the one-particle reduced density matrix (1-RDM) of a correlated wavefunction. They are ordered by occupation number, concentrating the correlation description into the fewest possible orbitals — ideal as an AEGISS initial guess.

NOs always use the full orbital space. To freeze core orbitals use FNOs instead.

docs.title: 10. Frozen Natural Orbitals (FNOs)¶
docs.text:
FNOs partition the orbital space into a frozen core and an active set before performing the NO transformation. This reduces the cost for larger systems by excluding deep core orbitals from the correlated calculation.

Two keyword arguments control the partition — use whichever is more natural:

Argument Meaning frozen=list[int] Indices of occupied orbitals to exclude from correlation (recommended) active=list[int] Indices of occupied orbitals to include in correlation (complement view) active=True Include all occupied orbitals — equivalent to standard NOs (default)

When frozen is provided it takes precedence over active.

docs.title: Summary¶
docs.text:
Method localize key Criterion Typical use Boys "boys" Minimum orbital spread General purpose, π systems Pipek–Mezey "pm" Maximum atomic charge σ/π separation, transition metals Edmiston–Ruedenberg "er" / "edmiston" Maximum self-repulsion Rigorous, expensive IBOs "ibos" / "ibo" Maximum IAO population Transition metals, mixed bonding IAOs "iaos" / "iao" Minimal-basis projection Population analysis, IBO input Natural Orbitals "nos" Diagonalise full 1-RDM Pre-CASSCF guess Frozen NOs "fnos" Diagonalise virtual block of 1-RDM Active-space truncation FNOs (frozen core) "fnos" + frozen= Same, core excluded Heavy atoms, large systems

Frozen orbitals (frozen=list[int]) can be passed to "fnos". The listed orbitals are excluded from the correlated calculation but kept in the output, so mf.mo_coeff retains its full shape and the rest of the AEGISS pipeline requires no changes.

The localized mo_coeff can be passed to any subsequent AEGISS step by replacing mf.mo_coeff before calling select_aegiss or select_by_ao_projection. Keep in mind that the DMRG active region is a window of ncas orbitals taken by index around the occupied/virtual boundary: for canonical orbitals that is a Fermi-level window, but localized orbitals have no orbital energies and their order within the occupied and virtual blocks is arbitrary, so the same window no longer selects the frontier orbitals. Natural orbitals are ordered by occupation number, a different but meaningful criterion. Check that the window contains the orbitals you care about.

Next: 02_dmrg.ipynb — running the DMRG calculation and inspecting orbital entropies.

docs.title: Tutorial 2 — DMRG and Single-Orbital Entropies¶
docs.text:
This notebook shows how to configure and run a DMRG calculation with AEGISS, extract single-orbital entropies from the resulting MPS, and apply the entropy-based screening step.

Prerequisites: block2 must be installed. The rest of the AEGISS stack (PySCF, NumPy) is assumed available.

Contents

  1. Molecule and mean-field setup
  2. DMRGConfig — parameters explained
  3. Running DMRG and obtaining entropies
  4. Entropy-based orbital screening
  5. Visualising single-orbital entropies

docs.title: 2. Molecule and mean-field setup¶
docs.text: We use water (H₂O) for speed. The same workflow applies to any system — just adjust ncas and nelecas in DMRGConfig accordingly.

docs.title: 3. DMRGConfig¶
docs.text:
DMRGConfig defines the CAS and the DMRG solver settings.

Field Type Default Meaning ncas int — Number of active orbitals nelecas int or (int, int) — Active electrons (total or α/β pair) max_bond_dim int 500 Target bond dimension; must be a positive multiple of 4 symm_type 'SZ' or 'SU2' 'SZ' Spin symmetry. 'SZ' required for entropies verbosity int 0 block2 output level

Note: symm_type='SU2' is faster but cannot produce entropies directly. Use 'SZ' whenever you need the single-orbital entropies.

docs.title: 4. Identify the CAS orbital subspaces¶
docs.text: get_subspaces_from_cas partitions the CAS into occupied (active) and virtual orbital index arrays using the aufbau occupation from the mean-field object.

docs.title: 5. Run DMRG¶
docs.text:
run_dmrg_subprocess launches a block2main DMRG sweep schedule and returns:

  • energy — the DMRG ground-state energy
  • soe1 — single-orbital entropies \(S_1(i)\) for every orbital in the CAS

docs.title: 6. EntropyConfig and orbital screening¶
docs.text:
EntropyConfig controls which orbitals survive the entropy threshold:

Field Default Meaning fraction 0.1 Threshold value (see fraction_type) fraction_type 'r' 'r': keep if \(S_1 \geq\) fraction × max(S_1); 'a': keep if \(S_1 \geq\) fraction ranking 'subset' Apply threshold independently per subspace or globally

docs.title: 7. Tuning the threshold¶
docs.text: Increasing fraction makes the selection more restrictive; decreasing it is more inclusive. The 'global' ranking pools occupied and virtual orbitals before thresholding — useful when you expect the most entangled orbitals to span both spaces.

docs.title: 8. Visualise single-orbital entropies¶
docs.text: AEGISS provides soe_heatmap and th_plots to produce diagnostic PDFs. Here we do a quick inline bar chart using matplotlib.

docs.title: Summary¶
docs.text:
• DMRGConfig defines the CAS and DMRG solver parameters.
  • run_dmrg_subprocess returns soe1 — the per-orbital entanglement measure.
  • EntropyConfig + select_by_entropy filter the CAS down to the most correlated orbitals.
  • The screened orbital lists (screened_occ, screened_virt) feed directly into the AO projection step.

Next: 03_ao_projection.ipynb — selecting orbitals by their chemical character using AO projection.

docs.title: Tutorial 3 — AO Projection and Chemical Character Screening¶
docs.text:
After the DMRG entropy step has pruned the CAS down to the most entangled orbitals, AO projection refines the selection by asking: how much does each surviving orbital look like a specific atomic orbital group?

This notebook covers:

  1. How to obtain AO label strings — manually or via MolTagger
  2. ProjectionConfig — all parameters explained
  3. Running select_by_ao_projection directly
  4. Threshold mode (contribution + contribution_type)
  5. Top-N ranking mode (top_n)
  6. Per-group thresholds and multi-group selection
  7. Restricting the search to entropy-screened orbitals
  8. Visualising AO contributions

Prerequisites: PySCF and NumPy. block2 is not required for this notebook — the entropy-screened space is simulated directly.

docs.title: 1. Obtaining AO label strings¶
docs.text:
AO labels follow the PySCF mol.search_ao_label convention:

"<Element> <shell>"          # e.g. "C 2pz", "Fe 3d", "O 2p"
"<Atom index> <Element> <shell>"  # pin to a specific atom, e.g. "0 C 2pz"
"<Element>.<tag> <shell>"        # atoms tagged with MolTagger, e.g. "C.1 2pz"

You can define them in two ways:

docs.title: Option A — by hand¶
docs.text:
Inspect the PySCF AO list and write the strings directly:

mol.ao_labels()          # list every AO in the molecule
mol.search_ao_label("C 2pz")  # verify which AOs match

docs.title: Option B — MolTagger (recommended for large molecules)¶
docs.text:
MolTagger (aegiss.utils.mol_tagger) provides an interactive 3D viewer where you click on atoms and get ready-to-paste ao_labels strings:

from aegiss.utils.mol_tagger import MolTagger

mol.tofile("molecule.xyz")            # MolTagger reads an XYZ file
tagger = MolTagger("molecule.xyz")
tagger.show()                         # opens the viewer; blocks until the window is closed

Note — run MolTagger from a standalone Python script or a terminal session, not from inside a Jupyter notebook: the viewer's Qt event loop blocks the kernel and the cell hangs.

After selecting the atoms of interest in the viewer, copy the suggested labels from the AO Labels panel. The tool auto-detects:

System Suggested labels Planar π system (benzene) "C 2pz" Non-planar organic (CH₄) "C 2p" with a warning Transition metal (Fe) "Fe 3d" Lanthanide (Ce) ["Ce 4f", "Ce 5d"] σ scaffold "C 2px", "C 2py", "C 2s", "H 1s"

The labels suggested by MolTagger are passed directly to ProjectionConfig(ao_labels=...) with no further editing needed.

docs.title: 3. Molecule and mean-field setup¶
docs.text: We use benzene as the working example: it has a clear π system (C 2pz) that should be captured by AO projection.

docs.title: Inspect the AO list¶
docs.text: Verify that "C 2pz" matches the expected AOs before building the config.

docs.title: 4. ProjectionConfig¶
docs.text:
ProjectionConfig collects all AO projection settings.

Field Type Default Meaning ao_labels list[str \| list[str]] — AO groups to project onto basis str \| None 'minao' Basis for projection (None → use molecule basis) contribution float \| list[float] 0.5 Weight threshold (or per-group list) contribution_type 'a' or 'r' 'a' 'a' = absolute; 'r' = relative to max weight top_n int \| list[int] \| None None Keep top-N orbitals per group instead of thresholding ranking 'subset' or 'global' 'subset' Apply projection per subspace or on combined set

ao_labels format: a flat string selects one group; a nested list ["Fe 3d", "Fe 4d"] treats both shells as a single group (contributions are summed). Groups are processed independently and their results unioned.

docs.title: 5. Running AO projection (no entropy pre-screening)¶
docs.text:
select_by_ao_projection can be called without a restricted_space argument to screen directly over all MOs. This is useful for a quick sanity check.

Over all MOs, a 0.5 absolute cut picks up the six π MOs plus a high-lying virtual (MO 52) with C 2p_z character — one reason to restrict the search to the entropy-screened window (section 9).

docs.title: 6. Threshold modes: absolute vs relative¶
docs.text:
The weight \(w_p^D = \sum_{\eta \in D} |[\mathbf{O}_E^D]_{\eta p}|\) is an L1 norm of the projected MO coefficients over the AO group \(D\).

  • contribution_type='a' (absolute): keep orbital \(p\) if \(w_p^D \geq \epsilon\). Useful when you have a physical intuition for the expected weight scale.

  • contribution_type='r' (relative): normalise all weights by \(\max_p w_p^D\) and keep orbital \(p\) if \(w_p^D / \max \geq \epsilon\). The threshold is now dimensionless and in [0, 1] — easier to tune across different systems.

docs.title: 7. Top-N ranking mode¶
docs.text: Instead of a threshold you can request the top N orbitals by weight. This guarantees a fixed number of orbitals per group regardless of the weight distribution — useful when you know the target CAS size in advance.

docs.title: 8. Multiple AO groups¶
docs.text:
Pass multiple entries in ao_labels to screen against several chemical characters simultaneously. The final active space is the union of orbitals selected by each group.

You can supply:

  • A single threshold applied to all groups
  • A per-group threshold list (one value per group)
  • A per-group top_n list

Example: select π carbons and the σ C–H bonds.

docs.title: Grouped labels (multi-shell metals)¶
docs.text:
For transition metals and f-block elements you often need to group multiple shells into a single AO entry — the contributions are summed before thresholding. MolTagger does this automatically for lanthanides and actinides.

# Cerium: treat 4f + 5d as a single group
ao_labels = [["Ce 4f", "Ce 5d"]]

# Iron porphyrin: three independent groups
ao_labels = ["Fe 3d", "N 2p", "C 2pz"]

docs.title: 9. Restricting to the entropy-screened space¶
docs.text:
In the full AEGISS pipeline the AO projection step operates only on the orbitals that survived entropy screening. Pass restricted_space as the (screened_occ, screened_virt) tuple returned by select_by_entropy: two lists of (orbital_index, entropy) pairs.

Here we simulate that step with the CAS(18e, 18o) window from get_subspaces_from_cas, which returns plain index arrays, so we wrap them as pairs first.

docs.title: ranking parameter¶
docs.text:
ranking is a ProjectionConfig field used by select_aegiss. select_by_ao_projection itself has no such argument: it treats an (occ, virt) tuple as a single pool.

ranking Behaviour in select_aegiss 'subset' (default) Occupied and virtual survivors are projected separately, each with its own threshold 'global' Both are merged and projected once, with a single threshold over the combined pool

'subset' is usually preferable: with a relative threshold it keeps the largest weight in one subspace from setting the cut for the other.

docs.title: 10. Visualising AO contributions¶
docs.text: Pass save_path to write a contribution heatmap to disk. save_path is a base path without extension: _heatmap.pdf is appended automatically. This is especially useful when debugging multi-group selections for large transition-metal systems.

docs.title: Direct control: plot_ao_contribution¶
docs.text: save_path uses sensible defaults. For finer control, pass return_contributions=True to get the per-group AO contributions back alongside the selected indices, then call the plotting function yourself:

docs.title: Summary¶
docs.text:
• AO label strings follow the PySCF mol.search_ao_label format. MolTagger can generate them automatically from an interactive 3D viewer.
  • ProjectionConfig centralises all AO projection settings: ao_labels, basis, contribution, contribution_type, top_n, ranking.
  • contribution_type='a' applies an absolute weight cutoff; 'r' normalises by the maximum weight first.
  • top_n guarantees a fixed number of orbitals per group.
  • Per-group thresholds and per-group top_n lists allow fine-grained control in multi-group selections.
  • restricted_space=(screened_occ, screened_virt) limits the search to the entropy-screened pool from the previous step.

docs.title: Tutorial 4 — Complete AEGISS Workflow¶
docs.text:
This notebook ties together everything from the previous three tutorials into a single end-to-end run of the AEGISS active space selection pipeline.

What you will do

  1. Build a molecule and run a mean-field calculation
  2. (Optional) Localise the orbitals
  3. Configure the four AEGISS objects: DMRGConfig, EntropyConfig, ProjectionConfig, OutputConfig
  4. Call select_aegiss — the single function that runs DMRG, entropy screening, and AO projection
  5. Interpret the result and inspect saved artefacts
  6. Explore threshold sensitivity and multi-group AO labels

Working example: benzene (C₆H₆) in cc-pVDZ. DMRG runs in a CAS(18e, 18o) window around the Fermi level, and AEGISS narrows it down to the π system. The correct answer is well known — six π MOs — so you can immediately verify the pipeline.

Prerequisites: block2, PySCF, NumPy.

docs.title: 2. Build the molecule¶
docs.text: We use benzene in the cc-pVDZ basis — small enough for a fast DMRG run, large enough to show meaningful entropy variation across the π and σ spaces.

docs.title: 4. (Optional) Orbital localization¶
docs.text:
Localization is not required, but it can improve physical interpretability of the entropy landscape — particularly for transition-metal systems where canonical MOs are delocalized over the whole ligand field.

For benzene we skip localization: the canonical π MOs are already well separated and the C 2pz AO projection correctly identifies them from canonical orbitals.

To use localized orbitals, replace mf.mo_coeff before calling select_aegiss:

# Boys localization of the occupied space
mf.mo_coeff = localize("boys", mol, mf)

# Pipek–Mezey (preserves σ/π separation)
mf.mo_coeff = localize("pm", mol, mf)

# Natural Orbitals from MP2
mf.mo_coeff = localize("nos", mf, correlated_method="mp2")

The DMRG window is taken by orbital index around the occupied/virtual boundary, which is a Fermi-level window only for canonical orbitals: after localization, check that it still contains the orbitals you care about.

See 01_scf_and_localization.ipynb for a detailed comparison of all localization schemes.

docs.title: 5. Configure the four AEGISS objects¶
docs.text: The full pipeline is driven by four frozen dataclasses. Configure them once; pass them all to select_aegiss.

docs.title: 5a. DMRGConfig — CAS and solver settings¶
docs.text:
Field Meaning ncas Number of active orbitals nelecas Active electrons (total int or α/β tuple) max_bond_dim Target bond dimension; must be a positive multiple of 4 symm_type 'SZ' or 'SU2'; both give spin-summed entropies, 'SZ' is required for UHF and spin-resolved entropies verbosity block2 output level (0 = silent)

The window must be larger than the active space you expect. Benzene's six π MOs are 16, 19, 20 (occupied) and 21, 22, 29 (virtual): a canonical CAS(6e, 6o) window covers only MOs 18–23, so MOs 16 and 29 could never be selected. CAS(18e, 18o) covers MOs 12–29.

docs.title: 5b. EntropyConfig — entropy-based orbital screening¶
docs.text: Field Default Meaning fraction 0.1 Threshold value (interpretation depends on fraction_type) fraction_type 'r' 'r': keep if \(S_1 \geq\) fraction × max(S_1); 'a': keep if \(S_1 \geq\) fraction ranking 'subset' Apply threshold independently per subspace ('subset') or jointly ('global')

docs.title: 5c. ProjectionConfig — AO projection-based screening¶
docs.text:
Field Default Meaning ao_labels — AO groups to project onto (PySCF ao_labels strings) basis 'minao' Minimal basis used for the projection contribution 0.5 Weight threshold (or per-group list) contribution_type 'a' 'a' = absolute weight cutoff; 'r' = relative to per-group maximum top_n None Select the top-N orbitals per group instead of thresholding ranking 'subset' Apply per subspace ('subset') or on the combined pool ('global')

For benzene we target the π system with "C 2pz". The six π MOs each have a large weight on the carbon 2p_z AOs and should all pass the threshold.

docs.title: 5d. OutputConfig — files and plots¶
docs.text: Field Default Meaning saving_folder './aegiss_output/' Directory for cube files and PDFs saving_prefix 'aegiss_selection' Filename prefix save_orb True Write cube files for the entropy-screened and final orbitals save_plots False Write diagnostic PDFs (SOE heatmap, TH plot, AO-contribution heatmaps, composition pie chart)

docs.title: 6. Run the full AEGISS pipeline¶
docs.text:
select_aegiss orchestrates the entire workflow in one call:

  1. Identifies the CAS orbital subspaces from dmrg_config
  2. Runs the DMRG calculation and extracts single-orbital entropies
  3. Applies the entropy threshold (entropy_config) → screened_occ, screened_virt
  4. Projects the surviving orbitals onto the AO groups (projection_config) → final active space
  5. Saves cube files and diagnostic PDFs if requested (output_config)

Returns: a sorted np.ndarray of integer orbital indices.

docs.title: 7. Interpret the result¶
docs.text: With the CAS(18e, 18o) window and "C 2pz" projection we expect six π MOs — the three bonding (occupied: 16, 19, 20) and three antibonding (virtual: 21, 22, 29) π orbitals. These are the orbitals responsible for aromaticity and strongly correlated character of the π system.

docs.title: 8. Saved artefacts¶
docs.text:
When save_orb=True, AEGISS writes cube files for:

  • Orbitals that passed entropy screening (*_entropy_<index>.cube)
  • The final AEGISS active space (*_AEGISS_<index>.cube)

The index in the file name follows the configured orbital index base.

When save_plots=True, these diagnostic PDFs are written:

  • *_SOE_heatmap.pdf — heatmap of the per-orbital single-orbital entropies
  • *_TH_plot.pdf — entropy threshold curve across the window orbitals
  • *_occ_heatmap.pdf, *_virt_heatmap.pdf — AO-contribution heatmaps of the projection step, one per subspace with ranking='subset'
  • *_composition_alpha.pdf — AO composition pie charts of the final orbitals

docs.title: 9. Inline entropy bar chart¶
docs.text: A quick visual check that the entropy profile matches expectations before inspecting the saved PDFs. The cell re-runs the DMRG to get the entropies (a few seconds).

docs.title: 10. Tuning the entropy threshold¶
docs.text: A sweep over fraction shows how the size of the active space changes. The plateau at six orbitals, from 1 % to 20 % of the maximum entropy, confirms that the π MOs are well separated from the rest of the window by entropy. At 50 % only the four frontier π MOs (19–22) survive.

docs.title: 11. Multi-group AO labels: π + σ¶
docs.text:
To capture both the π system and the C–H σ bonds, pass two AO groups in ao_labels. The final active space is the union of orbitals selected by each group.

Use per-group thresholds when the expected weight scales differ between groups (here π weights are larger than σ weights on the minimal basis).

For benzene the result is the same as π-only. AO projection only sees the orbitals that survived entropy screening, and the C–H σ orbitals are not entangled enough to pass it, so the "H 1s" group has nothing to pick from. A second AO group pays off when the entropy step leaves several kinds of orbitals.

docs.title: Multi-shell metals¶
docs.text:
For systems where two shells should be treated as a single group (their contributions are summed before thresholding), nest them in a list:

# Iron porphyrin — three independent groups
projection_config = ProjectionConfig(
    ao_labels=["Fe 3d", "N 2p", "C 2pz"],
    contribution=[0.4, 0.2, 0.2],
    contribution_type="a",
)

# Cerium complex — 4f + 5d treated as one group
projection_config = ProjectionConfig(
    ao_labels=[["Ce 4f", "Ce 5d"], "N 2p"],
    top_n=[5, 3],
)

MolTagger (aegiss.utils.mol_tagger) generates these strings automatically from an interactive 3D viewer — click atoms, copy labels.

docs.title: 12. Top-N mode¶
docs.text: When you know the target CAS size in advance, top_n guarantees exactly that many orbitals per group regardless of the weight distribution. It can be combined with multi-group and per-group lists.

docs.title: Summary¶
docs.text:
Step Function / object Key parameter Build molecule build_mol atom, basis Mean-field run_scf method ('RHF', 'RKS', …) (Optional) Localize localize 'boys', 'pm', 'er', 'ibos', 'iaos', 'nos', 'fnos' DMRG DMRGConfig ncas, nelecas, symm_type='SZ' Entropy screening EntropyConfig fraction, fraction_type, ranking AO projection ProjectionConfig ao_labels, contribution / top_n Output OutputConfig saving_folder, save_orb, save_plots Run pipeline select_aegiss all four configs

The returned active_indices array contains the sorted orbital indices that define the final active space — ready to pass to a CASSCF or CASCI solver.

docs.title: Tutorial 5 — Unrestricted (UHF) references¶
docs.text:
The first four tutorials use a restricted (RHF) reference. This short tutorial collects what changes when the reference is unrestricted (UHF), so you can reuse the same AEGISS workflow on open-shell and spin-polarised systems. It does not re-derive the theory — see the UHF reference page for the single-orbital-entropy formalism.

We use the benzene radical cation (charge=1, spin=1) as a genuinely open-shell running example (α and β occupations differ).

docs.title: Differences at a glance¶
docs.text: Stage Restricted (RHF) Unrestricted (UHF) Mean field run_scf(mol, method="RHF") run_scf(mol, method="UHF") mf.mo_coeff 2-D (nao, nmo) 3-D (2, nao, nmo) — α/β blocks DMRGConfig any symm_type symm_type="SZ" required; unrestricted autodetects; spin_soe controls SOE FCIDUMP restricted IUHF=1 (αα/ββ/αβ blocks) Single-orbital entropy 4-state spatial S(1) spin-summed (same 4-state) or spin-resolved per-spin-orbital H(n_α),H(n_β) select_by_ao_projection np.ndarray split {"alpha", "beta"} dict restricted_space / contribution scalar / list may also be a per-channel {"alpha", "beta"} dict select_aegiss np.ndarray split {"alpha", "beta"} dict (α and β not reconciled)

docs.title: 2. Mean field — the only structural change¶
docs.text: Build an open-shell molecule (charge/spin flow straight through to PySCF) and ask for a "UHF" mean field. The single observable difference is that mf.mo_coeff becomes 3-D (2, nao, nmo) — separate α and β blocks. Everything downstream keys off that shape.

docs.title: 3. DMRGConfig for UHF¶
docs.text:
Three fields matter for an unrestricted run:

  • symm_type="SZ" — required. UHF breaks \(\hat S^2\) symmetry, so the spin-adapted "SU2" solver is rejected.
  • unrestricted — None (default) autodetects UHF from the mean field; True/False overrides. When active it writes an IUHF=1 FCIDUMP.
  • spin_soe — how single-orbital entropies are computed: "summed" (4-state spatial S(1) → one spatial space), "resolved" (per-spin-orbital H(n_α), H(n_β) → α and β screened independently), or "auto" (picks "resolved" when nα ≠ nβ).

Resolve the effective choice with DMRGConfig.spin_resolved().

docs.title: 4. Single-orbital entropy: summed vs resolved¶
docs.text:
With spin_soe="summed" the entropy is the usual 4-state spatial S(1) and screening yields one orbital list. With spin_soe="resolved" AEGISS uses the per-spin-orbital binary entropy

\[ H(n_{i\sigma}) = -n_{i\sigma}\ln n_{i\sigma} - (1-n_{i\sigma})\ln(1-n_{i\sigma}), \]

computed from the 1-PDM diagonal (exact for a single spin-orbital by particle-number symmetry), and screens the α and β channels separately. The two are related by subadditivity \(\;|H_i^\alpha - H_i^\beta| \le S_i^{\text{spatial}} \le H_i^\alpha + H_i^\beta\); the resolved form discards the intra-orbital α–β (double-occupancy) correlation. See the UHF reference page for the full treatment and a block2 cross-check.

docs.title: 5. AO projection returns a split dict¶
docs.text: select_by_ao_projection detects the 3-D mo_coeff and screens each spin block against the same (spin-independent) AO overlaps, returning a {"alpha", "beta"} dict. This step needs no DMRG, so it runs here directly.

docs.title: Per-channel thresholds and windows¶
docs.text: For a UHF reference both contribution and restricted_space accept a per-channel {"alpha", "beta"} dict, letting you cut the two spin channels differently (a non-dict value is shared by both). Here β is held to a stricter relative cut than α:

docs.title: 6. Full pipeline — select_aegiss¶
docs.text:
select_aegiss wires DMRG + entropy + AO projection together. For a UHF reference it returns the same split {"alpha", "beta"} mapping; the α and β selections are kept separate (an orbital index means a different MO in each channel, so they are deliberately not reconciled).

This cell drives a DMRG solve through the block2main subprocess, so run it in an environment where block2 is installed (it is not executed when building these docs):

docs.title: Recap¶
docs.text:
Going unrestricted touches only the edges of the workflow:

  1. run_scf(..., method="UHF") → 3-D mo_coeff.
  2. DMRGConfig(symm_type="SZ", spin_soe=...) — everything else autodetects.
  3. Selection functions return a split {"alpha", "beta"} dict instead of one array, and per-channel contribution / restricted_space dicts are available.

The α and β spaces are two independent index lists, never merged: an unrestricted CAS needs as many α as β orbitals, so check the two lengths before building it (see The UHF active space). For the entropy theory and a numerical validation against block2, see the UHF reference page.
